before.title: Fable: icon map, icon packs and icon pack designer
before.detail: FABLE build, fresh on current main, replacing the stale icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app (about 2,003 behind; archive the old record and close its PR, branch kept). Icon map: every icon spot in every app (icons, badges, app icons) has an address. Icon packs: swap any or all of them at once, per app or hub-wide, with reset. Icon Pack Designer: a very powerful, polished, easy drag-and-drop editor to build a pack against the map; drag icons onto spots, live preview across the apps. Randomly generated icon sets (generate a whole pack or one icon with a style). Import icons from many sources (open icon libraries, uploaded SVG/PNG, URLs, other packs). Tokens and framework controls, console-control addresses, MCP/CLI/voice control. Land through the orchestrator.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 34 steps (9 Fable).

origin.said: Yes, use Fable too. I want a very powerful, nice, easy to use drag and drop, and also have random generated ones and import icons from different sources. Make it use Fable. Make it sick.

split.note: Split by Claude into 34 steps (9 Fable).

steps.text: Retire the stale build: archive the icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app record in the builds store with a note pointing to this build, and close its PR through the push banner (keep the branch). Check overlapping open builds (icon-pack-studio-fable, skins-asset-types) and record merge or clash notes on them.

Design the icon-map@1 contract. An address is <app>/<surface>/<spot>, and each spot has a kind (icon, badge or app-icon), a default glyph, a size role and a tone role. Write the address grammar, the scope chain (hub → app → screen → plugin, child overrides parent) and the reset rules.
steps.why: Cross-port contract and address scheme every app's icon spots depend on

steps.text: Add the icon-map and icon-pack asset types to the registry: the icon-pack holds glyph sources (svg, png, ref, generated), spot assignments and a style. Add a skin declaration (by: reference, via skin.iconPack), then regenerate the JSON Schemas.
steps.why: Schema design in the single source of truth for asset types

steps.text: Write the icon-pack migration: turn existing iconPack references and older icon-map data into the icon-pack format (versioned and lossless), with a dry-run report.
steps.why: Schema migration design

steps.text: Reference engine, part 1: build the icon-map registry engine (register spots, list them by app/surface/kind, validate addresses) in framework/core.
steps.why: Engine internals for a cross-port contract

steps.text: Reference engine, part 2: add resolveIcon(address, scopes). It walks the pack chain from hub to app to screen to plugin, falls back to the default glyph, supports reset per spot, per pack and per scope, and returns the source plus compiled tone and size tokens.
steps.why: Engine internals: scope resolution shared by every app

steps.text: Design the import normalizer contract: sanitize SVG (strip scripts, handlers and external refs), set viewBox and currentColor so tokens apply, cap PNG size, and load icons by URL or by naming an open library icon (lucide, tabler, material-symbols, phosphor) through a source registry that more libraries can be added to.
steps.why: Security-relevant cross-port contract for icon data

steps.text: Design the generator contract: a seeded generator (style: line, solid, duotone, rounded, geometric or pixel; stroke; corner; density) that turns a seed and a spot's meaning into an SVG built from primitives. It can make one icon or a whole pack, gives the same output for the same seed on every port, and colours only through tokens.
steps.why: Engine internals with a determinism contract across ports

steps.text: Change framework/react's Icon and Badge so they take an address (prop or data-axf-icon), resolve through the runtime's icon map, and hot-swap with runtime.swap('icon-pack', id). Add rt.iconMap to the runtime.
steps.why: Changes how GUIs render icons across every app

steps.text: Generate fixtures for the registry, resolveIcon, import sanitizing and seeded generation. Add the check script, and record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap (Android is on hold).
steps.why: Conformance contract for engines on both ports

steps.text: Ship the starter assets: the default icon-map with every framework spot, plus default, outline and duotone icon-packs. Add them to the shared asset set and bake them.
Map the Dev Console's icon spots: change console nav, banners, toolbars, plugin badges and the app icon to use addresses, and register the console's spots.
Map the icon spots in axHub web, AmberX web, Molly and Expenses (addresses plus app-icon spots), then re-bake them with rebake.mjs.
Add a CI check (check-icon-map.mjs) that fails on any icon or badge without an address and any address missing from the map. Keep a ratchet baseline whose counts can only go down.

Add a pack store to the icon-packs plugin: the per-app active pack in each app's app-look@1, the hub-wide pack on the shared appearance document, and screen and plugin scopes. Add reset per spot, pack and scope, with one undo.
Add REST routes for the icon-packs plugin: map list and get, pack list, get, create, update, delete and duplicate, use and reset per scope, resolve an address, import, and generate.
Add a CLI that matches the REST routes: node framework/cli/icon-packs.mjs map|list|get|use|reset|resolve|import|generate|export.

Expose the same actions as MCP tools through plugin-commands and as AmberX voice console actions (iconpack.use, iconpack.reset, iconpack.assign, iconpack.generate, iconpack.import, iconpack.open), plus control@1 targets for pack tokens, appended at the end of the registry.

Designer shell: add the icon-pack-designer plugin with its plugin.json (builtWith, lifecycle, install.mjs and uninstall.mjs), a view registered under Settings → Plugins, and a three-pane layout of spot map, canvas and sources, built with framework controls and tokens only.
Designer spot map pane: a tree of every spot grouped app → surface → kind, with search, filters (unassigned, overridden, badges, app icons), per-spot reset, and multi-select.
Designer drag and drop, part 1: drag an icon from the sources pane onto a spot or onto a multi-selection to assign it, with drop-target highlights, keyboard alternatives, and tap-to-place on touch.
Designer drag and drop, part 2: swap two spots by dragging between them, drag a whole source set onto a surface to fill it by matching names, and add undo/redo history.

Designer live preview: render real app surfaces (console nav, banner, toolbars, axHub, AmberX and Molly mock frames) under the pack being edited, switch between desktop and phone, and pass every theme and skin swap through.
Designer sources pane, open libraries: search lucide, tabler, material-symbols and phosphor through the import engine, with a preview grid and drag to place.

Designer sources pane, uploads and URLs: drop SVG or PNG files, paste a URL or raw SVG, borrow icons from other packs, run everything through the sanitizer with clear errors, and let saved custom icons be reused.

Designer generator panel: pick a style, lock or reroll the seed, generate one icon for the selected spot, fill only empty spots, or generate a whole pack. Show a variant strip to pick from, every result can be dragged, and generation is wired to the REST, CLI, MCP and voice generate actions.

Designer pack toolbar: new, duplicate, rename, save, export and import a pack file, use the pack (this app, hub-wide, screen or plugin), and reset. Make it a Toolbars plugin toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label, tap-to-confirm), with a confirm on destructive actions.

Designer polish: an empty state, a coverage meter (spots assigned out of total), a contrast warning for each theme, a first-run hint, and right-click on any icon in any app to edit it in the Icon Pack Designer, which opens the designer at that address.

Designer API: add console-control addresses for the view, spot rows, sources, the generator and the toolbar (console_show / console_open deep links such as view:icon-pack-designer?spot=<address>), and a readable state endpoint (current pack, selection, preview app). Register them with data-axf-target and make check-console-control pass.

Appearance integration: add an Icons section to Settings → Appearance (AppearancePanel) with the pack picker for each scope, reset, and Open designer. Let skins reference iconPack, so skin-coverage reports icons as covered.
Describe both plugins and the CLI where they are defined so the glossary covers them. Add notify.json entries for pack-applied alerts and help stubs.

Tests: Python route tests (sanitizer rejects hostile SVG, scope reset, generate is deterministic), CLI tests, and Playwright tests of the designer drag and drop on mouse and touch. Run check-icon-map, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets and the plugin lifecycle uninstall checks.
Submit to UI Review: designer desktop and phone shots, with 3 layout options shipped as assets in plugins/icon-pack-designer/assets/, through review.mjs submit --choices, group named after the build.

Finish: run the full checks (fixtures, tracker --check, builds-store verify), write the report _claude/builds/reports/fable-icon-map-icon-packs-icon-pack.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR. The PR says how each feature is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and that it is waiting in UI Review. Link it with builds-live.mjs link, and land it through the merge queue.

before.detail: FABLE build, fresh on current main, replacing the stale icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app (about 2,003 behind; archive the old record and close its PR, branch kept). Icon map: every icon spot in every app (icons, badges, app icons) has an address. Icon packs swap any or all of them, per app or hub-wide, with reset. Icon Pack Designer: very powerful, polished, easy drag-and-drop editor against the map with live preview. Randomly generated icon sets (whole pack or one icon in a style). Import icons from many sources (open icon libraries, SVG/PNG upload, URLs, other packs). Tokens, framework controls, console-control addresses, MCP/CLI/voice. Land through the orchestrator.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 33 steps (10 Fable).

origin.said: Yes, use Fable too. I want a very powerful, nice, easy to use drag and drop, and also have random generated ones and import icons from different sources. Make it use Fable. Make it sick.

split.note: Split by Claude into 33 steps (10 Fable).

steps.text: Write the icon map address contract (icon-map@1). Every icon spot (icon, badge, app icon) gets a stable address in the form app/screen/spot, plus its kind and a default glyph. Add or extend the icon-map and icon-pack entries in asset-types.json, regenerate the JSON Schemas, and write the spec doc.
steps.why: New cross-port asset-type contract and schema design

steps.text: Define the icon-pack@1 format: glyph entries (SVG or a reference to another glyph), the style block (stroke, corner, fill, palette as tokens), where each icon came from and its licence, and whether the pack is partial or full. Add the TS and mjs validators that check it.
steps.why: Schema design for a shared asset type

steps.text: Build the core of the icon map engine. It keeps a registry of addresses and resolves each one through the scopes in order: hub, then app, then screen, then plugin, with the closer scope winning, matching the skin and icon-map scope model. It also does reset per scope or per spot and returns a diff of what changed.
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Migrate the existing icon packs and icon-map scope data to icon-map@1 and icon-pack@1 (a migration function plus a dry-run report) and keep the old ids working.
steps.why: Migration design for existing assets

steps.text: Build the random generator engine. From a seed it makes the same result every time: either a whole pack or a single icon in a given style. Style values (stroke, corner, fill, palette) come only from tokens. It also supports locking icons so they keep their glyph when the rest is regenerated.
steps.why: Engine internals with a deterministic cross-port contract

steps.text: Build the import normalizer engine. It cleans SVG (no scripts, event handlers or outside references), sets a standard viewBox, maps colours to currentColor and tokens, wraps PNGs into an SVG container, and turns a glyph from another pack into a reference to it.
steps.why: Engine internals and a security-sensitive shared contract

steps.text: Generate golden fixtures for icon-map, icon-pack, icon-gen and icon-import and add a tsx conformance check. Record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md, since Android work is on hold.
steps.why: Cross-port conformance fixtures

steps.text: Wire icons in framework/react through the map. Add an <Icon address> / IconSlot component that registers its address, sets data-axf-icon, resolves the glyph through the runtime and hot-swaps it. Add runtime.icons with get, swap and reset.
steps.why: Changes how icons render in every app

steps.text: Update the framework controls to use addressed icons: Button, IconButton, Badge, TabGroup, banner chips, nav menu items and the app icon slot.
steps.why: Changes GUI behaviour across every app

steps.text: Add a CI check that fails on any icon render without an address. Add the icon-pack declaration to skin coverage and update ratchet baselines where needed.
steps.why: Cross-app enforcement contract

steps.text: Archive the stale build icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app in the builds store with a note naming this build, and close its PR as a veto call. Keep its branch.

Build the map scanner CLI (framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan|list|check). It walks the console, axHub web, AmberX, Molly and Expenses sources and writes the generated icon map registry, which is then baked into the shared assets.
Move the remaining raw icon uses in the console views onto addressed <Icon> spots, starting with the views that have the most.
Move the remaining raw icon uses in the console plugins and other app sources onto addressed spots, then re-bake the apps with rebake.mjs.
Scaffold the icon-pack-studio plugin: plugin.json (builtWith, description, uiEditor), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, lifecycle dataDir, notify.json, and a README.

Add the server routes: read the map, list, get, create, update and delete packs, apply a pack at a scope (hub, app, screen, plugin, one spot), reset with an undo token, and preview-diff. Applying writes through the hub appearance and app-look documents.
Add the import source routes: open icon libraries (Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor, Material Symbols, Heroicons) with search and licence info, plus a server cache of results.

Add the remaining import routes: SVG and PNG upload, fetch from a URL (guarded against requests to internal addresses, with size and type limits), and copy from another pack. All of it goes through the import normalizer.
Add the random generation routes: a whole pack, one icon in a style, regenerating with locked icons kept, and a seed history.
Build the studio UI shell: the plugin view with a framework TabGroup (Map, Packs, Import, Generate), a toolbar with role=toolbar and an id, and a split layout. Tokens and framework controls only.
Build the map tree: apps, then screens, then spots, with search and filters by kind (icon, badge, app icon), an override marker per spot, and a reset per node from the right-click menu.

Build the pack canvas: a glyph grid and drag-and-drop from the library, uploads or generated icons onto map spots or the grid. Include multi-select, swap by dragging one spot onto another, undo/redo, and a touch long-press drag fallback.

Build the live preview pane: it applies the draft pack to a chosen app and screen in a framed preview, with a desktop/phone toggle and highlighting of the spot under the cursor. It switches through runtime.icons.swap without saving.
Build the Import tab UI: library browser with search and licence badges, an upload drop zone, a URL field, and a picker for other packs. Results can be dragged straight onto the canvas.
Build the Generate tab UI: style sliders (stroke, corner, fill, palette tokens), a seed field with a dice button, lock icons, generate one or all, and seed history.

Build the per-icon editor dialog: rename, replace, style overrides from tokens, and where the icon came from. Add the Apply dialog: a scope picker (hub, app, screen, plugin), a diff of what changes, apply, and Reset to default with a confirm and one undo.
Add a Settings → Plugins → Icon Pack Studio sub-tab (default source, licence filter, preview app, auto-apply) with the level toolbar, chrome settings ids and Install & uninstall panel.

Add the API, part 1: console-control addresses (view, tab, map spot, pack row, setting) registered via data-axf-target, and console_show / console_open deep links for the studio, a spot, a pack and the tabs. State is readable through REST /api/console-control.

Add the API, part 2: plugin commands for MCP (icons map/list/get/apply/reset/import/generate/swap-spot), console actions for AmberX voice (icons.apply, icons.reset, icons.randomize, icons.import), the CLI `axf icons …`, and control@1 entries for icon tokens. All four do the same things.
Ship three starter packs as assets (one hand-picked, one generated from a seed, one partial pack for badges only) and add descriptions for the glossary and help stubs.

Write the tests: pytest for routes, importers (including the URL guard and SVG sanitizing) and generation; tsx tests for the map tree, dnd reducer and apply/reset round-trip. Run check-icon-map, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle --after-uninstall and the glossary catalog --check.
Take desktop and phone shots of the studio (map, canvas mid-drag, preview, import, generate) and submit them to UI Review as kind app with three studio layout options as assets (ui-choices@1).

Final step: run the full check sweep, write the report at _claude/builds/reports/icon-pack-studio-on-fable.md (what replaced the stale build, the API reach table for REST/MCP/CLI/voice, known gaps), add the THREADS row, push the branch, open the PR stating that UI Review is waiting and how each feature is reached, link it with builds-live.mjs, and add it to the merge queue.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 29 steps (8 Fable).

origin.said: Use Fable. Very powerful, nice, easy drag and drop, random generated ones, import icons from different sources. Make it sick.

steps.text: Archive build icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app and close its PR: note it was replaced by icon-pack-studio-fable in the builds store (orchestrator.mjs act status archived + note), close the PR with a comment through github-token.mjs, and record the replacement in the build's origin addendum

Survey what already exists on main for icons (icon map engine, iconPack on skin@1, icon assets, Icon component, skin-coverage icon parts) and write the design note listing reused pieces vs new contracts
steps.why: Sets the cross-app icon contract every later step builds on

steps.text: Design icon-spot@1: every place an icon is drawn gets a stable spot id (app, view, control, role) and a registry; add the icon-spot schema to asset-types.json and regenerate JSON Schemas
steps.why: New shared asset type / schema used by every app

steps.text: Design icon-pack@1 (glyphs: svg path / svg source / png data / url ref, viewBox, stroke/fill mode, tags, source provenance, extends another pack) and icon-source@1 (library, upload, url, pack, generator) in asset-types.json; regenerate schemas
steps.why: Schema design for a shared asset type with provenance

steps.text: Scope + reset model: icon pack selection hub-wide → app → screen → plugin with child-overrides-parent, per-spot overrides, Restore to default with one undo; migration from the existing skin iconPack field and any icon-map settings keys
steps.why: Migration design and cross-app resolution rules

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/icon-packs.ts: resolveIcon(spot, scopes) with fallback chain, pack merge (extends), validation, and SVG sanitising (strip scripts, events, external refs) for imported glyphs
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Seeded random generator engine framework/core/engines/icon-gen.ts: deterministic icons from a seed (geometric primitives, stroke weight and corner style from theme tokens) and whole-pack generation that covers every registered spot role
steps.why: Engine internals: deterministic output is a conformance contract

steps.text: Fixtures: framework/spec/fixtures/icon-packs.json (resolution, scope inheritance, reset, sanitising) and icon-gen.json (seed → output), wired into gen-fixtures.mts; Android twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Framework wiring: Icon component resolves through the icon-packs engine by spot id, glyph colours and sizes from --fx-* tokens only; runtime swap of the active pack (runtime.swap('icon-pack', id)); skin-coverage reads the new type
steps.why: Changes how icons render in every app

steps.text: Starter assets: default icon pack built from the current icons (no visual change) plus two contrasting packs in framework/assets/icon-pack/; register in shared-assets.json and bake

Icon spot scanner framework/cli/icon-map.mjs: lists every icon spot in console, axHub web, AmberX, Molly, Expenses (static scan of Icon usages + registry), writes the icon map, and a --check mode that fails on an icon without a spot id
Give spot ids to remaining Icon usages in the console views and framework controls the scanner flags (ratchet baseline only goes down)
Plugin scaffold apps/console-web/plugins/icon-pack-studio: plugin.json (builtWith, description, uiEditor), install.mjs/uninstall.mjs, lifecycle dataDir, Settings → Plugins sub-tab, help stub

Server routes server/routes.py: list/read/create/update/delete packs, pick pack per scope, per-spot override, reset/undo, icon map read, generate (seed), all through the icon-packs engine semantics; pack data in the plugin dataDir and the hub appearance document

Import routes: from bundled icon libraries (open-licensed sets already vendored or fetched by name with licence recorded), SVG/PNG upload (size cap, sanitise, PNG → data glyph), URL fetch (https only, size/type limits, SSRF guard), and copy from another pack
Server tests for routes + importers: sanitiser rejects scripts, URL guard blocks private hosts, reset/undo round trip, generate is deterministic

Icon Map view: grid of every spot grouped by app/view with the current glyph, which scope set it, filter/search, click a spot to override; framework controls + DataGrid + TabGroup only; registers console-control targets
Pack manager view: packs as cards with live mini previews, apply to hub / app / screen / plugin, Restore to default with confirm and undo; console-control targets and data-axf-target on every action

Icon Pack Designer, part 1: three-pane layout (source tray, pack grid of spot slots, live preview of real console chrome), drag a glyph from tray onto a slot (pointer + touch drag, keyboard alternative), toolbar with role=toolbar and settings id
Icon Pack Designer, part 2: reorder/swap slots by drag, drop files and URLs straight onto slots, multi-select, undo/redo stack, per-glyph tweaks (stroke, fill mode, padding) bound to tokens
Designer live preview: preview pane renders sample console banner, toolbar, nav and buttons through the Icon component with the draft pack scoped in, swapping theme updates it live
Random generator UI: Randomise one slot / fill empty slots / generate whole pack, seed shown and lockable, shuffle history to step back, style knobs (geometry family, weight, rounding)
Import panel UI: tabs for Icon libraries (search + drag results into tray), Upload SVG/PNG, From URL, From another pack; licence/provenance shown per glyph

API parity: console_show deep links for map, manager, designer, a pack and a spot; state reads; plugin-commands MCP tools for every route; console actions iconpack.* for voice (AmberX); control@1 targets for pack picks
CLI parity: node framework/cli/icon-packs.mjs list|show|use|override|reset|undo|generate|import|map, calling the console API with the same semantics; usage header comment for the glossary

Engine + UI checks: framework/spec/check-icon-packs.mts (engine vs fixtures, generator determinism), add icon-map.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control and check-chrome-assets passing for the plugin; wire into CI
Rebake console, axHub web and AmberX with the new framework + shared assets (rebake.mjs, shared-assets.mjs bake), run typecheck and builds
UI Review: shots of Icon Map, Pack manager and Designer (desktop + phone) with 3 option assets for the designer layout, submit via review.mjs --choices with group 'icon-pack-studio-fable - <date>'

Tests, report and PR: run all checks above plus tracker.mjs --check and plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall; write _claude/builds/reports/icon-pack-studio-fable.md (what replaced the old build, contracts, API reach per feature), THREADS row, open the PR naming REST/MCP/CLI/voice/deep link for each feature, link it with builds-live.mjs and hand it to the merge queue

# Build: attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-16T22:44:59.053Z
> Rebuild.

## What to build
Continue build "Attach widgets to any toolbar, banner style" (attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-16 22:44):
"Rebuild."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (5 left, ~41 min):
[ ] s1 (~8 min) Survey current main for intent and seams: read the archived branch diff (git log/diff of toolbar-widgets-attach-any-banner-style) for intent only, plus framework/core/engines (banner widget host, attach/snap rules), framework/react/tapConfirm.ts, framework/ui/axf.css banner section, schemas/customize.json style targets; write the design note _claude/builds/reports/attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner.design.md (contract, settings keys, addresses) and commit

CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.

- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.

- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. steps.why: Starts the Fable phase that designs the cross-app widget-host contract

steps.text: Map what already exists on main: banner widget host engine, widget style/shape options (banner-widget-shapes), attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner work, Toolbars plugin toolbar settings and the attached-things snap rule in axf.css. Add a short 'Current state' section to the report listing the files and what is missing for toolbars
steps.why: Gap analysis for a contract change that affects every app's toolbars

steps.text: Contract: extend the widget-host contract so a toolbar is a widget host like a banner (host kind 'toolbar', slots start/end/overflow, per-widget style + shape taken from the banner widget style registry, attach order). Write it in framework/spec (widget host section) and add the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md
steps.why: Cross-port contract for how widgets attach to every app's toolbars

steps.text: Schema: add the toolbar widget fields (widgets[] with id, slot, style, shape, order) to the toolbar entry in framework/schemas/asset-types.json, validators following it, then regenerate JSON Schemas (node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas). Old toolbars with no widgets stay valid (migration = no-op, recorded)
steps.why: Asset type schema change and migration design

steps.text: Engine part 1: in the widget host engine (framework/core/engines), accept host kind 'toolbar' and resolve a widget's style and shape from the banner widget style/shape registry, the same way for both host kinds (one function, no copy)
steps.why: Reference engine internals shared by banners and toolbars

steps.text: Engine part 2: snap-not-overlap layout for toolbar hosts: widgets and buttons size to their content, the flexible item shrinks to its minimum first, then overflow (scroll snap or More); pure function returning placements, no DOM
steps.why: Engine layout rule that changes GUI behaviour across apps

steps.text: Fixtures: add toolbar-host cases to the widget host fixtures (each banner widget style and shape on a toolbar, crowded toolbar snap/overflow, empty toolbar, old asset with no widgets), regenerate with npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts and check them with npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-widgets.mts
steps.why: Conformance fixtures are the cross-port contract

steps.text: React: render the attached widgets in the framework toolbar (role=toolbar hosts) through the shared banner widget component, with the resolved style and shape, using framework controls and --fx-* tokens only; tap-to-confirm stays on toolbar buttons and does not wrap widgets

CSS: toolbar widget slots in framework/ui/axf.css on the attached-things rule (content sizing, min-width shrink, sideways scroll snap); tokens and color-mix opacity only, no px literals; run node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs and check-controls.mjs

Attach UI: the toolbar's context menu (Toolbars plugin and ChromeContext) gets 'Add widget…' (picker of every widget), and each attached widget gets Style, Shape, Move (slot/order) and Remove, saved to the toolbar asset's widgets[] per toolbar settings id
Drag and drop: dropping a widget (drop-target@1) on any toolbar attaches it at the drop slot; dragging it out removes it; the snap-not-overlap placement is applied live

Console-control addresses: register each toolbar's widget slots and attached widgets as targets (toolbar:<id>/widget:<wid>) through data-axf-target or the framework controls, append-only in the control registry; node framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs passes

API (REST): Toolbars plugin routes GET toolbars/<id>/widgets (state), POST attach, PATCH style|shape|move, DELETE detach, all validated against the schema and writing the same settings as the UI; deep link view to open a toolbar's widget editor for console_show / console_open

API (MCP + console actions + voice): register the actions toolbar.widget.list|attach|style|shape|move|detach (plugin commands / console actions, read automatically as MCP tools), voice phrases for AmberX, with a description on each
API (CLI): axf toolbar widgets <id> [attach|style|shape|move|detach] in framework/cli calling the same routes, with a help header; check that the CLI, REST, MCP and voice give the same results

Re-bake the framework into the shared-asset apps (node framework/cli/rebake.mjs apply for the console, then shared-assets.mjs bake) so every app's toolbars get it; chrome-settings check and check-toolbars.mjs pass
Tests: engine tests for the toolbar host (style/shape resolution, snap/overflow), a plugin route test (attach → read → move → detach), and action parity across REST, MCP, CLI and voice

UI Review: shots on desktop and phone of a toolbar with widgets in at least 3 banner styles/shapes, 3 option assets (choices file) under apps/console-web/plugins/toolbars/assets/, submit with review.mjs submit --choices --group 'toolbar-widgets-in-any-banner-style - <time>'

Wrap-up: run validate --framework, check-widgets, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, check-chrome-assets, tracker --check; finish the report _claude/builds/reports/toolbar-widgets-in-any-banner-style.md (what changed, how each feature is reached: deep link, state, REST, MCP, CLI, voice), THREADS row, push the branch, open the PR saying the UI Review is waiting, link it with builds-live.mjs link

notes.text: Split by Claude into 16 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: Rebuild.

split.note: Split by Claude into 16 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the widget shape + icon override contract: add `shape` (circle | square | rounded | pill | hexagon | custom with a custom path/mask ref) and `icon` override fields to the banner widget / widget-host entry in asset-types.json, with defaults that keep today's circle, and write the migration note (no field = circle, no icon override = the widget's own icon)
steps.why: Schema design for a shared asset type used by every app's banner

steps.text: Regenerate JSON Schemas and extend the JS/TS validators so shape values, the custom-shape reference and the icon override are checked (unknown shape refused with the field named)
steps.why: Validator contract shared across ports

steps.text: Widget host engine: resolve per-widget shape and icon (per-widget setting > widget asset > banner default), compile shape into tokens (`--fx-widget-radius`, clip-path / mask for hexagon and custom) taken from the style theme radius tokens, never fixed px
steps.why: Engine internals that change how banner widgets draw in every app

steps.text: Add fixtures for shape + icon resolution (each shape, custom, inheritance order, missing icon falls back) and regenerate golden outputs; record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Extend check-widgets.mts to cover the new fields (engine vs fixtures, validators agree, runtime host API exposes setShape/setIcon) and run it green
Style the shapes in the base stylesheet from the compiled tokens only (square, rounded, pill, hexagon, custom mask), keeping attached-things-snap rules so no shape clips a neighbour
React banner widget renderer: apply the resolved shape class/tokens and the icon override through the framework Icon component; keep role/aria and data-axf-target on each widget
Per-widget settings: add Shape (Segmented of the shapes + custom picker) to the widget's settings in the banner chrome settings interface asset, stored as `axf.banner.widget.<id>.shape`

steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Engine part 2: compile resolved icons into tokens (--fx-icon-* size/stroke/tone from the theme, glyph URLs / inline SVG ids), sanitise SVG (strip scripts, handlers, external refs) in framework/core/engines/icon-sanitize.ts
steps.why: Engine internals plus a security contract for imported SVG

steps.why: Changes how icons render in every app

Starter packs: ship default, outline, filled and one generated pack as icon-pack assets in framework/assets/icon-pack/, baked through shared-assets.mjs bake
Plugin scaffold: apps/console-web/plugins/icon-packs (plugin.json with builtWith, install.mjs, uninstall.mjs, lifecycle dataDir, settings sub-tab under Settings → Plugins, notify.json)

Server routes: apps/console-web/plugins/icon-packs/server (list spots, read map, get/put/delete pack, apply pack to app/hub/screen/plugin, reset, generate, import from source with fetch allow-list + size limit + sanitise)
Import adapters on the server: open library fetchers (Lucide, Tabler, Material Symbols, Phosphor via their npm/CDN packages), PNG to data URL, URL import with SSRF guard, pack-to-pack copy; tests

Designer UI part 1: Icon Pack Designer layout on framework controls: spot map tree (by app, screen, kind) left, pack canvas centre, icon library and sources right, TabGroup for Library / Import / Generate
Designer UI part 2: drag-and-drop (mouse, touch, keyboard) from library or imports onto spots, onto whole groups, onto the pack; multi-select; undo/redo; drop-target@1 hooks
Designer UI part 3: live preview pane rendering real console screens (and other apps) with the pack in progress, theme-swap aware, phone and desktop sizes, before/after toggle
Designer UI part 4: Generate tab (style, seed, shuffle, lock spots, regenerate one or all, generate whole pack) and Import tab (search libraries, upload SVG/PNG, paste URL, pick from another pack)

Apply and reset UI: per-app / hub-wide / screen / plugin apply with confirm, Reset spot, Reset app, Reset to default with one undo; right-click on any icon in any app → Change icon… opens the designer at that spot

API parity: console-control targets (view:icon-packs, spot:<id>, pack:<id>) via data-axf-target, control@1 entries appended last, plugin-commands MCP tools, `axf icons …` CLI (list, show, apply, reset, generate, import, export), AmberX voice actions icons.apply/reset/generate/open
Settings and Appearance: Settings → Appearance icon-pack picker joins the skin iconPack reference; level toolbar settings for the plugin (default pack, generator style, allowed sources)
Glossary + help: descriptions on plugin, commands, assets, CLI header; help stub; catalog.mjs --check

Tests: fixtures check, check-skin-coverage, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, icon-spots --check, plugin-lifecycle --after-uninstall, plugin server tests, console typecheck + build
UI Review: desktop + phone shots of the Designer, Generate, Import and Apply views, submitted with 3 asset options via review.mjs submit --choices (group named after the build)

Finish: write _claude/builds/reports/icon-packs-with-drag-drop-pack-designer.md (what landed, API reach per feature: deep link, state, actions, settings over REST/MCP/CLI/voice), update the THREADS row, open the PR and link it with builds-live.mjs link

steps.text: Design the icon-map@1 and icon-pack@1 asset types in framework/schemas/asset-types.json: icon-map = spot registry (id, kind, app, default glyph, size token, tint token, tags); icon-pack = glyph set (svg|png|font|ref sources, per-spot and per-name entries, extends, license/source per glyph, generator seed). Place them before uac-policy; set skin coverage (icon-pack: by reference via skin.iconPack; icon-map: none with why). Regenerate schemas (axf.mjs schemas)
steps.why: New shared asset types = schema design

steps.text: Design icon-scope@1 resolution: hub-wide pack -> app pack -> screen (ui:<view>) -> plugin scope, child overrides parent, per-spot overrides on top, reset per spot / per app / hub-wide; storage keys in the appearance@1 / app-look@1 documents (icon.pack, icon.scopes, icon.overrides). Document it in framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md and ICON-MAP.md with migration from any existing iconPack field
steps.why: Cross-app scope + migration design

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/icon-pack.ts: validate a pack, fold extends chains (inherit@1), resolve(spot, scopes) -> glyph + source + which scope won, list overrides, reset ops returning new documents. Pure TS, no DOM
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Engine framework/core/engines/icon-map.ts: build the spot registry from icon-map assets plus runtime registrations (rt.registerIconSpot), dedupe, coverage report (spots with no glyph in a pack), search by tag/kind/app
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Deterministic icon generator engine framework/core/engines/icon-gen.ts: seeded SVG glyph builder (shape grammar: primitives, symmetry, stroke/fill from theme tokens via currentColor, no literal colours), generateIcon(seed, hints) and generatePack(seed, spots, style) with stable output so fixtures hold
steps.why: Engine internals with golden fixtures, must match on every port

steps.text: SVG sanitizer + import normalizer engine framework/core/engines/icon-import.ts: strip scripts/handlers/external refs, normalise viewBox and size, map fills to currentColor, PNG -> data URI with size cap, record source + license metadata. Shared by upload, URL and library imports
steps.why: Engine internals + security contract for imported glyphs

steps.text: Validators: add icon-map and icon-pack checks to framework/core/project-check.mjs / the asset validator so axf.mjs validate --framework covers them; mjs mirror where the rules engines hard-code spec lists
steps.why: Schema contract validators

steps.text: Fixtures: add cases to framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts for resolve/scopes/reset, coverage, generator seeds and sanitizer; generate framework/spec/fixtures/icon-pack.json, icon-gen.json, icon-import.json; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md (Android on hold)
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

> When the orchestrator assigns builds or steps they are sent to the right employee who has its own set of briefs to send back to the orchestrator and uses the employee data in the brief. In the group chat the orchestrator asks if anyone can do something, if they have skills or tools or capabilities; the first one to take it opens a dialog listing all the matching agents with a percentage of each one being the best choice for the job. After the 90 second veto it chooses the best probable one by default.

## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator assigns builds/steps to employee agents via group chat, with match % dialog and 90 s veto" (orchestrator-assigns-builds-steps-to-employee-ag) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 16:28):
"When the orchestrator assigns builds or steps they are sent to the right employee who has its own set of briefs to send back to the orchestrator and uses the employee data in the brief. In the group chat the orchestrator asks if anyone can do something, if they have skills or tools or capabilities; the first one to take it opens a dialog listing all the matching agents with a percentage of each one being the best choice for the job. After the 90 second veto it chooses the best probable one by default."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

# Build: always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Always fill every slot: when slots are free, run independent steps of running builds in parallel across them, and auto-queue pending builds" (always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are) — Phase 2, model Opus.
This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

before.title: Landing auto-resolves generated files (no more clashes)
before.detail: Most Nov 13 land failures were clashes only in GENERATED or additive files: apps/console-web/src/control/inventory.json, framework/assets/help/framework.json and every baked copy (apps/*/src/assets/help/framework.json, apps/*/src/axf/assets/help/framework.json), framework/catalog/status.json, framework/spec/PORTING.md, framework/spec/fixtures/*.json, framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts outputs, apps/*/axf.lock.json, and the baked framework copies under apps/*/src/axf/. Fix the land path (/opt/axf-batch/resolve.py used by vps.build_land, and the orchestrator lander): (1) list generated files in one manifest; (2) on a clash in a generated file, take main's side, then run the matching generator (control inventory, help bake, fixtures, lock, framework re-bake) on the merged tree and commit; (3) additive docs/catalogs (PORTING.md, catalog status.json) are union-merged by key; (4) only real source clashes stop the land; (5) run tests after regeneration. Then re-land these waiting branches: full-voice-control-merge-main-and-land, skin-config-panel-merge-main-and-land, skins-plugin-merge-main-and-land, project-create-mcp, project-duplicate-boilerplate, drive-live-console-first, rename-long-builds, overlay-preview-ui-review. Must land before auto-land-every-finished-build-lands.

before.title: Watchdog + watch-rule system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, everything)
before.detail: A server-side watchdog on the VPS that runs every few minutes, checks every orchestrator table (pending, queued, building, merge queue, UI Review) for rows whose build has already landed on main or is otherwise done, and removes or marks them complete automatically. Logs each cleanup and sends an FYI to AmberX.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

origin.said: I want a server fucking watchdog on the VPS to do that.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Design the stale-row contract stale-row@1 in framework/core/stale-rows.mjs: a pure classifier that takes a row (pending, queued, building, merge-queue entry, UI Review item) plus facts (PR merged on main, commits on main, build status complete/failed/cancelled, branch deleted, PR closed) and returns keep | complete | remove with a reason code. Add framework/schemas/stale-row.json for the cleanup log record (row kind, row id, build id, action, reason, evidence, at, by: watchdog)
steps.why: New cross-table contract and log schema that every orchestrator table and the console read

steps.text: Write fixture cases for the classifier (landed via merge queue, landed by direct merge commit, closed unmerged PR, build complete but row still queued, UI Review item whose PR merged, a running build that must stay, a missing-facts row that must stay) plus a check script
steps.why: Fixtures are the contract for the classifier

steps.text: Facts gatherer: framework/cli/stale-facts.mjs reads origin/main (git log --merges, branch heads) and the GitHub PR states through github-token.mjs with ETag caching, so a run costs almost no API calls; returns one facts map keyed by build id / branch / PR
Table readers for builds-store rows: pending, queued and building projections from _claude/builds/store.json via builds-store.mjs, each mapped to classifier input

Table readers for the merge queue (land.mjs queue list / merge-queue.mjs state) and UI Review items (review.mjs list), mapped to classifier input; reached through the capabilities, not folder names, where the framework calls them

Watchdog core apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog.mjs: run = gather facts, read every table, classify, and with --dry-run only print the plan; settings (enabled, interval minutes, dry-run, per-table on/off) in the plugin settings registry

Apply actions: builds store rows marked complete with the merged PR (builds-live.mjs so main sees it at once), merge-queue entries removed through land.mjs queue remove, UI Review items closed as merged; every write under the store lock and journalled, never touching a running build

Cleanup log: append each action as a stale-row@1 record to the plugin dataDir (watchdog/log.jsonl, rotated monthly) plus a build note on the affected build; also a Codebase changes log line per run that did anything

FYI to AmberX: one batched notification per run that cleaned something (count + row list), declared in the plugin's notify.json (notify-types@1) and sent through axf.notify@1 so the Notifications panel controls it
VPS schedule: cron axf-stale-watchdog every 5 minutes running watchdog.mjs run with a lockfile so runs never overlap; install/uninstall in the plugin's install.mjs / uninstall.mjs
Health check: register a health@1 check in the systems check (watchdog last run older than 3 intervals or last run failed = red banner item with Auto fix that reruns it / reinstalls the cron)

API: REST routes /api/plugins/build-orchestrator/watchdog (GET status + last runs + log, POST run, POST dry-run, PUT settings), MCP via plugin-commands (watchdog-status, watchdog-run, watchdog-log, watchdog-settings), CLI axf watchdog status|run|log|set, voice actions orchestrator.watchdog.*

UI: a Watchdog card in Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (settings, last run, Run now, Dry run) and a Cleanups log tab using framework controls and TabGroup; register console-control targets (view:…/tab:watchdog, setting:…) and console_show deep link

Tests: unit tests for table readers and apply actions against a temp store, merge-queue and UI Review fixtures (dry-run makes no writes, running builds untouched, second run is a no-op); wire check-stale-rows.mjs into CI

Run checks (check-stale-rows, watchdog tests, builds-store verify, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle check, glossary catalog --check), dry-run on the VPS data and paste its plan, UI Review submit with 3 options, write _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-stale-row-watchdog-vps.md, add the THREADS.md row, open the PR saying how REST/MCP/CLI/voice reach each part

Shared watch-rule engine on the VPS: rules = a pre-built thing to watch + conditions combined with AND / OR (with grouping) + a pre-built action, with values chosen from lists. Reusable by any screen; the stale-row cleanup becomes the first built-in rule.
Collapsible 'Watches' section on the Build orchestrator page listing its rules (expandable rows, on/off, last fired), with an 'Add watch' button.

'Add watch' wizard, zero typing: a grid of pre-built things to watch; selecting one expands the row to pick pre-built conditions and actions from lists and enter values (dropdowns, pickers, number steppers). Plain-English summary of the rule before saving.

AND / OR conditions per watch: '+ add condition' in the wizard, each joined by an AND/OR picker, plus condition groups (e.g. (A AND B) OR C) built by clicking, no typing; the plain-English summary shows the logic.
Same collapsible 'Watches' container with the Add-watch wizard on the Plan Studio page, with Plan Studio's own pre-built things to watch and actions.

A master collapsible 'All watches' container listing every possible thing that can be monitored across the system (orchestrator, Plan Studio, UI Review, merge queue, accounts, VPS, etc.), grouped by area, each addable with one click via the same wizard.

Gates tab in the Watchdog panel: lists every existing gate on the VPS (test gate on landing, UI Review gate, merge approval, budget caps, etc.) as expandable rows with on/off, what it blocks, last triggered; plus 'Add gate' using the same zero-typing wizard (pre-built things to check, AND/OR conditions, pre-built block/notify actions).

Watchdog panel has exactly three tabs: 1) Watches (things being monitored + actions, incl. stale-row cleanup), 2) Gates (everything that blocks/holds work), 3) Rules (every standing rule the VPS enforces, e.g. account routing, auto-merge, rebuild-on-conflict, step splitting). Each tab: count in the tab label, expandable rows, on/off, and an Add button using the same zero-typing wizard.

Move Claude account selection out of the orchestrator: a VPS rules service decides which account each build runs on (orchestrator just asks it before starting a session). Move all existing account-routing options from console Settings (Claude accounts routing, subscriptions-first, per-account queued/parallel limits, etc.) into the Rules tab as pre-built rules, remove them from the old settings screen, keep routing-test preview working, and make sure no build ever starts without an account during the switch.

before.title: Replace merge queue with one-at-a-time landing
before.detail: Brett overrides the Nov 4 'only the queue merges' rule. Remove the batched/stacked merge queue (push-banner land.mjs rounds) and replace it with a serial lander: take one finished build, merge origin/main into it, regenerate generated files (generated-files@1), run its checks once, merge it to main, then the next. No stacking builds on each other, so a fix to one never restarts the others' tests. A cancelled CI run (superseded by a push) is never counted as a failure. On a red check, auto-file a fix build and move on to the next build instead of blocking the line. Show the landing line and its current build in the console with full API and voice control (pause, skip, move up). Redeploy the console after each landing batch. Tests, help, Shipped features.

Remove the batched/stacked merge queue (push-banner land.mjs rounds) and replace it with a serial lander: take one finished build, merge origin/main into it, regenerate generated files (generated-files@1), run its checks once, merge it to main, then the next. No stacking builds on each other, so a fix to one never restarts the others' tests. A cancelled CI run (superseded by a push) is never counted as a failure. On a red check, auto-file a fix build and move on to the next build instead of blocking the line. Show the landing line and its current build in the console with full API and voice control (pause, skip, move up). Redeploy the console after each landing batch. Tests, help, Shipped features.

# Build: replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-14T22:15:48.311Z
> We gotta get rid of that merge tier and start landing them one at a time

## What to build
Continue build "Replace merge queue with one-at-a-time landing" (replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-14 22:15):
"We gotta get rid of that merge tier and start landing them one at a time"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~30 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Design the landing-line@1 record and state machine: one ordered list of finished builds/PRs; states waiting → merging-main → regenerating → checking → landing → landed | fix-filed | skipped | paused; per-entry attempt log; CI conclusion mapping where cancelled/superseded = not a result (re-run, never a failure); one entry in flight at a time; no stacking. Write it as framework/core/landing-line.mjs (pure functions: next, transition, classifyCheckRun) plus a JSON Schema
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Migration design: convert the current merge queue (stacks, entries, queue/pr-* refs) into landing-line@1 entries in their old order, keep history, drop stack fields; write the migration as a pure function with a fixture (before/after JSON)
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Engine checks for landing-line@1: transitions, cancelled-run classification (cancelled / superseded / stale head = retry, failure / timed_out = red), red → fix-file + advance, pause / skip / move-up ordering, migration fixture
Read first: framework/core/landing-line.mjs, framework/schemas/landing-line.json, framework/spec/fixtures/landing-line-migrate.json, framework/spec/check-landing-line.mjs
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. steps.why: Conformance checks for the new contract

steps.text: Serial lander, part 1: apps/console-web/plugins/push-banner/land/lander.mjs takes the head entry, checks out its branch, merges origin/main into it, and sets the entry state; reuses the merge drivers already in land.mjs (builds files newer-wins, logs unioned)
Serial lander, part 2: run generated-files@1 regeneration (tracker, schemas, fixtures, help, exports) after the main merge and push the branch once (head pinned)

Serial lander, part 3: wait on the PR's checks for the pinned head; classify through landing-line.mjs; a cancelled or superseded run triggers one re-dispatch of the workflow and never counts as red; green merges the PR to main (merge commit naming the landing line) and advances

Red check handling: on a real failure, file a fix build in the orchestrator (pipeline.mjs intake with the failing check names, log excerpt, PR link and Brett's original words carried over), mark the entry fix-filed, link the fix build, then move on to the next entry

Run the migration on startup of the lander (old queue file → landing-line store, journalled), keep a read-only export of the old file for one release
Cron: the axf-auto-land cron runs `land.mjs run` as one landing pass (one entry per tick, lock file so ticks never overlap); queue-merging hold replaced by a landing-batch hold

REST API: /api/plugins/push-banner/landing (GET state: line, current build, its stage, last results; POST pause, resume, skip <id>, move-up <id>, add <pr>, remove <id>, run-now); lander settings (enabled, max re-dispatch on cancelled, auto file fix build) as settings keys
