Console UI, part 1: replace the push banner's Merge queue panel with a Landing line panel (framework DataGrid + TabGroup, tokens only): current build highlighted with its stage, ordered list, fix-filed and skipped rows with links
Console UI, part 2: a toolbar (role=toolbar, settings id) with Pause / Resume / Skip / Move up / Run now; row context menu with the same; banner chip shows 'Landing #N (stage)' or 'Paused'
Console control + deep links: register view:push-banner/landing, row:<pr>, and the toolbar buttons with control@1 (append-only), console_show/console_open targets; check-console-control passes
Settings sub-tab: Settings → Plugins → Push banner → Landing line (enabled, re-dispatch on cancelled, auto file fix build, redeploy after batch) through the settings asset; remove the stack settings

Systems check: health@1 item when the line is paused over an hour, a landing is stuck in one stage over 30 min, or a fix build was filed (banner item with Fix / Resume); notify.json entry for landing alerts

Rules and docs: replace 'Only the merge queue merges' in _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/rules/RULES.md and CLAUDE.md with the one-at-a-time landing rule (Brett, Nov 14 2026, his words); decision in _claude/memory/decisions.md; update the merge-queue memory doc; claude-sync sync

Help and glossary: help entries for the Landing line panel, commands and CLI; plugin.json and command descriptions; glossary-index catalog --check passes; Shipped features ledger rows for lander, API and UI

Tests for the lander: fake git + fake GitHub checks: green lands, cancelled run re-dispatches and is not red, red files a fix build and advances, pause/skip/move-up, one in flight at a time, redeploy once per batch
Route + command tests: REST, MCP, CLI and voice actions hit the same state; plugin-lifecycle check, check-toolbars, check-theme, check-controls, check-console-control
UI Review: 3 options for the Landing line panel as assets (ui-choices@1) with desktop + phone shots, submitted via review.mjs submit --choices

Finish: run the full check sweep (check-landing-line, lander tests, tracker --check, builds-store verify), write _claude/builds/reports/replace-merge-queue-one-time-landing.md (what was removed, API reach for each feature: deep link, state, actions, settings over REST/MCP/CLI/voice), THREADS row, push the branch and open the PR (this PR lands through the old queue one last time or by a single deliberate merge)

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

steps.text: Define the open-url route@1 contract that axHub, the console and AmberX share: try routes in order (connected console tab → full-screen intent or overlay exemption → notification), with inputs (url, host allowlist amberxai.com, foreground hint), the result shape {route, opened, reason}, and fixtures. steps.why: New cross-app protocol used by axHub, the console and the AmberX app

steps.text: Record the Android twin of open-url route@1 as a deferred gap in PORTING.md, and add the contract to the spec index.
steps.why: Cross-port contract bookkeeping for the new protocol

steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

AmberX settings: an 'Open pages' section showing permission status (overlay, full-screen intent) with grant buttons that deep-link to the Android settings screens, plus a test-open button. Built from framework controls and theme tokens only.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

Build the new AmberX APK in CI. On the S26 Ultra (through axHub), run amberx.open_url three times: Chrome in front with the console tab open, Chrome in front with no console tab, and the phone idle. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step fable-rebuild-to-do-manager-unlimited <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note fable-rebuild-to-do-manager-unlimited "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.

New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.

Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.

Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- Every rebuild ends with a differences report (Oct 20 2026): after any rebuild (Fable rebuilds and every future one, any model), write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/<pending-id>.md` comparing the new build with the version it replaced: what was removed, kept, changed and added; contract/API/asset/fixture changes; migrations and compatibility notes for apps already using it; tests before vs after; known gaps. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.

steps.text: Read the current todo-manager plugin (plugin.json, server, web UI, data files, commands) and the superseded build to-do-manager-fully-voice-mcp-controlled; write the design notes (current data shape, every entry point, the old build's notes folded in) into the report draft

steps.text: Read the archived branch claude/own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups for intent only (git log/diff, no merge) and write the design notes for this rebuild: what an instance token set is, which tokens it holds (row bg, alt row, text size, spacing, border width/colour, radius, hover, selected), and how it sits under the skin chain. Commit the notes.
steps.why: Sets the contract every grid and tab group across apps follows

steps.text: Add the instance-token-set@1 asset type to the registry (fields, allowed token keys per target kind grid|tab-group, the per-instance settings key axf.chrome.<kind>.<id>.tokens, skin coverage declaration) and regenerate JSON Schemas.
steps.why: New shared asset type and schema in the single source of truth

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/instance-tokens.ts: validate a set, resolve skin → app → instance with the child overriding the parent, compile to scoped --fx-* custom properties on the instance root (theme tokens only, opacity through --fx-opacity-*), and reset-to-skin = drop the instance layer.
steps.why: Engine internals that turn assets into tokens

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for instance-tokens (resolve, compile, reset, invalid keys refused), wire them into gen-fixtures, record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Add the starter assets: instance-token-set/default-grid and default-tab-group (empty = follow skin) plus two examples (compact-grid, pill-tabs), and validate the framework assets.
Add the React hook useInstanceTokens(kind, id) that reads the per-instance setting, keeps it fresh with useEditorSync, and returns the scoped style. Apply it on the TabGroup root.
Apply useInstanceTokens on the DataGrid root, and move the grid row, hover, selected, border and radius CSS onto the scoped tokens so an instance set restyles them with no edits.
Give every grid a stable settings id (data-axf-grid) and a right-click target (data-fx-ctx-target="grid"), add grid to the chrome-settings types, and add the settings/chrome-grid default asset.

Add the Look section to the chrome Settings… dialog for tab-group and grid: pick a token-set asset, edit each token with framework controls (colour, size, spacing, border, radius, hover, selected), live preview, Reset to skin with confirm and one undo.
Run chrome-settings backfill so every app in shared-assets.json plus Expenses gets its chrome-grid copy, and re-bake the console.

API part 1: register console-control addresses for each instance look (grid:<id>/look, tab-group:<id>/look, setting:axf.chrome.<kind>.<id>.tokens.<key>) and control@1 token targets, appended last in the registry.

API part 2: add console actions chrome.look.get | set | pick | reset | list (state read: which instances have their own set, resolved values), then a REST route under /api/console-control and MCP tools through plugin-commands.

before.title: Fable: icon map, icon packs and icon pack designer
before.detail: FABLE build, fresh on current main, replacing the stale icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app (about 2,003 behind; archive the old record and close its PR, branch kept). Icon map: every icon spot in every app (icons, badges, app icons) has an address. Icon packs: swap any or all of them at once, per app or hub-wide, with reset. Icon Pack Designer: a very powerful, polished, easy drag-and-drop editor to build a pack against the map; drag icons onto spots, live preview across the apps. Randomly generated icon sets (generate a whole pack or one icon with a style). Import icons from many sources (open icon libraries, uploaded SVG/PNG, URLs, other packs). Tokens and framework controls, console-control addresses, MCP/CLI/voice control. Land through the orchestrator.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 34 steps (9 Fable).

origin.said: Yes, use Fable too. I want a very powerful, nice, easy to use drag and drop, and also have random generated ones and import icons from different sources. Make it use Fable. Make it sick.

split.note: Split by Claude into 34 steps (9 Fable).

steps.text: Retire the stale build: archive the icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app record in the builds store with a note pointing to this build, and close its PR through the push banner (keep the branch). Check overlapping open builds (icon-pack-studio-fable, skins-asset-types) and record merge or clash notes on them.

Design the icon-map@1 contract. An address is <app>/<surface>/<spot>, and each spot has a kind (icon, badge or app-icon), a default glyph, a size role and a tone role. Write the address grammar, the scope chain (hub → app → screen → plugin, child overrides parent) and the reset rules.
steps.why: Cross-port contract and address scheme every app's icon spots depend on

steps.text: Add the icon-map and icon-pack asset types to the registry: the icon-pack holds glyph sources (svg, png, ref, generated), spot assignments and a style. Add a skin declaration (by: reference, via skin.iconPack), then regenerate the JSON Schemas.
steps.why: Schema design in the single source of truth for asset types

steps.text: Write the icon-pack migration: turn existing iconPack references and older icon-map data into the icon-pack format (versioned and lossless), with a dry-run report.
steps.why: Schema migration design

steps.text: Reference engine, part 1: build the icon-map registry engine (register spots, list them by app/surface/kind, validate addresses) in framework/core.
steps.why: Engine internals for a cross-port contract

steps.text: Reference engine, part 2: add resolveIcon(address, scopes). It walks the pack chain from hub to app to screen to plugin, falls back to the default glyph, supports reset per spot, per pack and per scope, and returns the source plus compiled tone and size tokens.
steps.why: Engine internals: scope resolution shared by every app

steps.text: Design the import normalizer contract: sanitize SVG (strip scripts, handlers and external refs), set viewBox and currentColor so tokens apply, cap PNG size, and load icons by URL or by naming an open library icon (lucide, tabler, material-symbols, phosphor) through a source registry that more libraries can be added to.
steps.why: Security-relevant cross-port contract for icon data

steps.text: Design the generator contract: a seeded generator (style: line, solid, duotone, rounded, geometric or pixel; stroke; corner; density) that turns a seed and a spot's meaning into an SVG built from primitives. It can make one icon or a whole pack, gives the same output for the same seed on every port, and colours only through tokens.
steps.why: Engine internals with a determinism contract across ports

steps.text: Change framework/react's Icon and Badge so they take an address (prop or data-axf-icon), resolve through the runtime's icon map, and hot-swap with runtime.swap('icon-pack', id). Add rt.iconMap to the runtime.
steps.why: Changes how GUIs render icons across every app

steps.text: Generate fixtures for the registry, resolveIcon, import sanitizing and seeded generation. Add the check script, and record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap (Android is on hold).
steps.why: Conformance contract for engines on both ports

steps.text: Ship the starter assets: the default icon-map with every framework spot, plus default, outline and duotone icon-packs. Add them to the shared asset set and bake them.
Map the Dev Console's icon spots: change console nav, banners, toolbars, plugin badges and the app icon to use addresses, and register the console's spots.
Map the icon spots in axHub web, AmberX web, Molly and Expenses (addresses plus app-icon spots), then re-bake them with rebake.mjs.
Add a CI check (check-icon-map.mjs) that fails on any icon or badge without an address and any address missing from the map. Keep a ratchet baseline whose counts can only go down.

Add a pack store to the icon-packs plugin: the per-app active pack in each app's app-look@1, the hub-wide pack on the shared appearance document, and screen and plugin scopes. Add reset per spot, pack and scope, with one undo.
Add REST routes for the icon-packs plugin: map list and get, pack list, get, create, update, delete and duplicate, use and reset per scope, resolve an address, import, and generate.
Add a CLI that matches the REST routes: node framework/cli/icon-packs.mjs map|list|get|use|reset|resolve|import|generate|export.

Expose the same actions as MCP tools through plugin-commands and as AmberX voice console actions (iconpack.use, iconpack.reset, iconpack.assign, iconpack.generate, iconpack.import, iconpack.open), plus control@1 targets for pack tokens, appended at the end of the registry.

Designer shell: add the icon-pack-designer plugin with its plugin.json (builtWith, lifecycle, install.mjs and uninstall.mjs), a view registered under Settings → Plugins, and a three-pane layout of spot map, canvas and sources, built with framework controls and tokens only.
Designer spot map pane: a tree of every spot grouped app → surface → kind, with search, filters (unassigned, overridden, badges, app icons), per-spot reset, and multi-select.
Designer drag and drop, part 1: drag an icon from the sources pane onto a spot or onto a multi-selection to assign it, with drop-target highlights, keyboard alternatives, and tap-to-place on touch.
Designer drag and drop, part 2: swap two spots by dragging between them, drag a whole source set onto a surface to fill it by matching names, and add undo/redo history.

Designer live preview: render real app surfaces (console nav, banner, toolbars, axHub, AmberX and Molly mock frames) under the pack being edited, switch between desktop and phone, and pass every theme and skin swap through.
Designer sources pane, open libraries: search lucide, tabler, material-symbols and phosphor through the import engine, with a preview grid and drag to place.

Designer sources pane, uploads and URLs: drop SVG or PNG files, paste a URL or raw SVG, borrow icons from other packs, run everything through the sanitizer with clear errors, and let saved custom icons be reused.

Designer generator panel: pick a style, lock or reroll the seed, generate one icon for the selected spot, fill only empty spots, or generate a whole pack. Show a variant strip to pick from, every result can be dragged, and generation is wired to the REST, CLI, MCP and voice generate actions.

Designer pack toolbar: new, duplicate, rename, save, export and import a pack file, use the pack (this app, hub-wide, screen or plugin), and reset. Make it a Toolbars plugin toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label, tap-to-confirm), with a confirm on destructive actions.

Designer polish: an empty state, a coverage meter (spots assigned out of total), a contrast warning for each theme, a first-run hint, and right-click on any icon in any app to edit it in the Icon Pack Designer, which opens the designer at that address.

Designer API: add console-control addresses for the view, spot rows, sources, the generator and the toolbar (console_show / console_open deep links such as view:icon-pack-designer?spot=<address>), and a readable state endpoint (current pack, selection, preview app). Register them with data-axf-target and make check-console-control pass.

Appearance integration: add an Icons section to Settings → Appearance (AppearancePanel) with the pack picker for each scope, reset, and Open designer. Let skins reference iconPack, so skin-coverage reports icons as covered.
Describe both plugins and the CLI where they are defined so the glossary covers them. Add notify.json entries for pack-applied alerts and help stubs.

Tests: Python route tests (sanitizer rejects hostile SVG, scope reset, generate is deterministic), CLI tests, and Playwright tests of the designer drag and drop on mouse and touch. Run check-icon-map, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets and the plugin lifecycle uninstall checks.
Submit to UI Review: designer desktop and phone shots, with 3 layout options shipped as assets in plugins/icon-pack-designer/assets/, through review.mjs submit --choices, group named after the build.

Finish: run the full checks (fixtures, tracker --check, builds-store verify), write the report _claude/builds/reports/fable-icon-map-icon-packs-icon-pack.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR. The PR says how each feature is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and that it is waiting in UI Review. Link it with builds-live.mjs link, and land it through the merge queue.

Icon map: every icon spot in every app (icons, badges, app icons) has an address. Icon packs swap any or all of them, per app or hub-wide, with reset. notes.text: Split by Claude into 33 steps (10 Fable).

origin.said: Yes, use Fable too. I want a very powerful, nice, easy to use drag and drop, and also have random generated ones and import icons from different sources. Make it use Fable. Make it sick.

split.note: Split by Claude into 33 steps (10 Fable).

steps.text: Write the icon map address contract (icon-map@1). Every icon spot (icon, badge, app icon) gets a stable address in the form app/screen/spot, plus its kind and a default glyph. Add or extend the icon-map and icon-pack entries in asset-types.json, regenerate the JSON Schemas, and write the spec doc.
steps.why: New cross-port asset-type contract and schema design

steps.text: Define the icon-pack@1 format: glyph entries (SVG or a reference to another glyph), the style block (stroke, corner, fill, palette as tokens), where each icon came from and its licence, and whether the pack is partial or full. Add the TS and mjs validators that check it.
steps.why: Schema design for a shared asset type

steps.text: Build the core of the icon map engine. It keeps a registry of addresses and resolves each one through the scopes in order: hub, then app, then screen, then plugin, with the closer scope winning, matching the skin and icon-map scope model. It also does reset per scope or per spot and returns a diff of what changed.
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Migrate the existing icon packs and icon-map scope data to icon-map@1 and icon-pack@1 (a migration function plus a dry-run report) and keep the old ids working.
steps.why: Migration design for existing assets

steps.text: Build the random generator engine. From a seed it makes the same result every time: either a whole pack or a single icon in a given style. Style values (stroke, corner, fill, palette) come only from tokens. It also supports locking icons so they keep their glyph when the rest is regenerated.
steps.why: Engine internals with a deterministic cross-port contract

steps.text: Build the import normalizer engine. It cleans SVG (no scripts, event handlers or outside references), sets a standard viewBox, maps colours to currentColor and tokens, wraps PNGs into an SVG container, and turns a glyph from another pack into a reference to it.
steps.why: Engine internals and a security-sensitive shared contract

steps.text: Generate golden fixtures for icon-map, icon-pack, icon-gen and icon-import and add a tsx conformance check. Record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in PORTING.md, since Android work is on hold.
steps.why: Cross-port conformance fixtures

steps.text: Wire icons in framework/react through the map. Add an <Icon address> / IconSlot component that registers its address, sets data-axf-icon, resolves the glyph through the runtime and hot-swaps it. Add runtime.icons with get, swap and reset.
steps.why: Changes how icons render in every app

steps.text: Update the framework controls to use addressed icons: Button, IconButton, Badge, TabGroup, banner chips, nav menu items and the app icon slot.
steps.why: Changes GUI behaviour across every app

steps.text: Add a CI check that fails on any icon render without an address. Add the icon-pack declaration to skin coverage and update ratchet baselines where needed.
steps.why: Cross-app enforcement contract

steps.text: Archive the stale build icon-map-icon-packs-every-icon-badge-app in the builds store with a note naming this build, and close its PR as a veto call. Keep its branch.

Build the map scanner CLI (framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan|list|check). It walks the console, axHub web, AmberX, Molly and Expenses sources and writes the generated icon map registry, which is then baked into the shared assets.
Move the remaining raw icon uses in the console views onto addressed <Icon> spots, starting with the views that have the most.
Move the remaining raw icon uses in the console plugins and other app sources onto addressed spots, then re-bake the apps with rebake.mjs.
Scaffold the icon-pack-studio plugin: plugin.json (builtWith, description, uiEditor), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, lifecycle dataDir, notify.json, and a README.

Add the server routes: read the map, list, get, create, update and delete packs, apply a pack at a scope (hub, app, screen, plugin, one spot), reset with an undo token, and preview-diff. Applying writes through the hub appearance and app-look documents.
Add the import source routes: open icon libraries (Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor, Material Symbols, Heroicons) with search and licence info, plus a server cache of results.

Add the remaining import routes: SVG and PNG upload, fetch from a URL (guarded against requests to internal addresses, with size and type limits), and copy from another pack. All of it goes through the import normalizer.
Add the random generation routes: a whole pack, one icon in a style, regenerating with locked icons kept, and a seed history.

before.detail: Fresh on main, replaces banner-widget-shapes-more-than-circle. Banner widgets get shapes beyond circle (square, rounded, pill, hexagon, custom), set per widget, plus a Change icon option per widget with an icon picker. Tokens, framework controls, console-control, MCP/CLI/voice. Land through the orchestrator.

notes.text: Split by Claude into 16 steps (4 Fable).

attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner (toolbar-widgets@1) reserves widgets[].shape (a shape@1 asset id per slot), toolbar.shape { icon, chip } defaults (same field as banner.shape) and data-fx-shape on toolbar widgets. The shape build resolves toolbars through the same chain; no second contract.

origin.said: Rebuild.

split.note: Split by Claude into 16 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the widget shape + icon override contract: add `shape` (circle | square | rounded | pill | hexagon | custom with a custom path/mask ref) and `icon` override fields to the banner widget / widget-host entry in asset-types.json, with defaults that keep today's circle, and write the migration note (no field = circle, no icon override = the widget's own icon)
steps.why: Schema design for a shared asset type used by every app's banner

steps.text: Regenerate JSON Schemas and extend the JS/TS validators so shape values, the custom-shape reference and the icon override are checked (unknown shape refused with the field named)
steps.why: Validator contract shared across ports

steps.text: Widget host engine: resolve per-widget shape and icon (per-widget setting > widget asset > banner default), compile shape into tokens (`--fx-widget-radius`, clip-path / mask for hexagon and custom) taken from the style theme radius tokens, never fixed px
steps.why: Engine internals that change how banner widgets draw in every app

steps.text: Add fixtures for shape + icon resolution (each shape, custom, inheritance order, missing icon falls back) and regenerate golden outputs; record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Extend check-widgets.mts to cover the new fields (engine vs fixtures, validators agree, runtime host API exposes setShape/setIcon) and run it green
Style the shapes in the base stylesheet from the compiled tokens only (square, rounded, pill, hexagon, custom mask), keeping attached-things-snap rules so no shape clips a neighbour
React banner widget renderer: apply the resolved shape class/tokens and the icon override through the framework Icon component; keep role/aria and data-axf-target on each widget
Per-widget settings: add Shape (Segmented of the shapes + custom picker) to the widget's settings in the banner chrome settings interface asset, stored as `axf.banner.widget.<id>.shape`

Change icon: add a 'Change icon…' item to each widget's right-click / long-press menu opening the framework icon picker (current icon pack aware), saved as `axf.banner.widget.<id>.icon`, with Reset to default
Backfill the per-app chrome-banner settings copies and run chrome-settings check + check-chrome-assets so every app carries the new fields

Console control: register targets `setting:banner.widget.<id>.shape`, `setting:banner.widget.<id>.icon` and the `chrome.widget-icon` dialog address (appended last in control@1), deep link opens the widget's settings / icon picker

API parity: console actions `banner.widget.shape` / `banner.widget.icon` / `banner.widget.reset` + state read (list widgets with shape and icon) through REST /api/console-control, MCP console_control_* and plugin commands
CLI + voice: `axf banner widget <id> shape <shape>|icon <name>|reset|list` and AmberX voice phrases mapped to the same actions; help entries
Re-bake the framework into the console and shared-asset apps (rebake.mjs, shared-assets bake) and run check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, theme-swap
UI Review: shoot desktop + phone of banner widgets in 3+ shape option sets and the Change icon picker, write each option as an asset under the owner plugin's assets folder and submit with --choices

steps.text: Design the icon-map@1 and icon-pack@1 asset types in framework/schemas/asset-types.json: icon-map = spot registry (id, kind, app, default glyph, size token, tint token, tags); icon-pack = glyph set (svg|png|font|ref sources, per-spot and per-name entries, extends, license/source per glyph, generator seed). steps.why: New shared asset types = schema design

steps.text: Design icon-scope@1 resolution: hub-wide pack -> app pack -> screen (ui:<view>) -> plugin scope, child overrides parent, per-spot overrides on top, reset per spot / per app / hub-wide; storage keys in the appearance@1 / app-look@1 documents (icon.pack, icon.scopes, icon.overrides). steps.why: Cross-app scope + migration design

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/icon-pack.ts: validate a pack, fold extends chains (inherit@1), resolve(spot, scopes) -> glyph + source + which scope won, list overrides, reset ops returning new documents. Pure TS, no DOM
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Engine framework/core/engines/icon-map.ts: build the spot registry from icon-map assets plus runtime registrations (rt.registerIconSpot), dedupe, coverage report (spots with no glyph in a pack), search by tag/kind/app
steps.why: Engine internals shared by every app

steps.text: Deterministic icon generator engine framework/core/engines/icon-gen.ts: seeded SVG glyph builder (shape grammar: primitives, symmetry, stroke/fill from theme tokens via currentColor, no literal colours), generateIcon(seed, hints) and generatePack(seed, spots, style) with stable output so fixtures hold
steps.why: Engine internals with golden fixtures, must match on every port

steps.text: SVG sanitizer + import normalizer engine framework/core/engines/icon-import.ts: strip scripts/handlers/external refs, normalise viewBox and size, map fills to currentColor, PNG -> data URI with size cap, record source + license metadata. Shared by upload, URL and library imports
steps.why: Engine internals + security contract for imported glyphs

steps.text: Validators: add icon-map and icon-pack checks to framework/core/project-check.mjs / the asset validator so axf.mjs validate --framework covers them; mjs mirror where the rules engines hard-code spec lists
steps.why: Schema contract validators

steps.text: Fixtures: add cases to framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts for resolve/scopes/reset, coverage, generator seeds and sanitizer; generate framework/spec/fixtures/icon-pack.json, icon-gen.json, icon-import.json; record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md (Android on hold)
steps.why: Cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Starter assets: framework/assets/icon-map/default.json (every spot from the inventory) and framework/assets/icon-pack/ default (current glyphs), outline, filled, and one generated pack; validate --framework; bake into shared apps (shared-assets.mjs bake) and check skin coverage (check-skin-coverage.mjs)
steps.why: Default assets for the new shared types

steps.text: Framework React: <AxfIcon spot=…> + useIconSpot in framework/react reading the resolved pack from the runtime (rt.icons), live hot-swap on pack/scope change, tokens only for size/tint; register spots automatically
steps.why: Changes how icons render in every app's GUI

Move the console's icon spots (nav, views, plugin badges, home cards, app icon/favicon) onto <AxfIcon spot>; register plugin spots through plugin.json icon fields
Move axHub web, AmberX web and Molly icon spots onto the framework; rebake each via rebake.mjs
CI check framework/cli/check-icon-spots.mjs: flags raw icon glyphs/SVGs outside <AxfIcon> with a ratchet baseline framework/spec/icon-baseline.json (counts only go down); wire into CI workflow

Drag and drop: drag glyphs from source tray / other packs / desktop files onto spots or the pack grid, drop onto a whole area to fill it, reorder, multi-select drag, touch drags (pointer events, drop-target@1), undo/redo stack
Live preview pane: render real app chrome samples (banner, nav, toolbar, badges, app icon at sizes) with the draft pack through a scoped runtime; phone/desktop toggle; before/after split
Source tray: tabs for Libraries (search), Upload, URL, Other packs, Generated; previews, license chips, add-to-pack
Generator panel: random icon / random whole pack with style hints (stroke, fill, rounded, geometric), seed lock, re-roll per spot, keep favourites

Apply & scope panel: apply pack hub-wide / per app / per screen / per plugin, per-spot overrides list, Reset spot / app / hub with confirm and one undo; Settings → Appearance link and chrome context menu entry 'Change icon…' on any icon

Console control: register targets (view:icon-packs, tabs, pack rows, spot rows, every button/setting) via data-axf-target; append control@1 targets last; console actions icon.pack.apply|icon.spot.set|icon.reset|icon.generate|icon.import; check-console-control.mjs passes

API parity: MCP plugin commands for every route, CLI node framework/cli/icon-packs.mjs (list|show|apply|set|reset|generate|import|coverage|open), AmberX voice intents, console_show deep links; state reads for designer draft and applied scopes
Help + glossary entries: plugin help page, descriptions on new assets, asset types and CLI; catalog.mjs --check and help ratchet clean

Tests: npx tsx framework/spec/check-icon-pack.mts (engines vs fixtures), plugin test.py (routes, sanitizer, SSRF guard, scopes, reset), lifecycle check --after-uninstall, theme-swap, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets

UI Review: desktop + phone shots of the designer, preview, generator and apply panel; submit with 3 choices (designer layout options as assets under plugins/icon-packs/assets/) via review.mjs submit --choices

Final: run validate --framework, tracker.mjs --check, check-skin-coverage, full test sweep; write _claude/builds/reports/icon-packs-with-drag-drop-pack-designer.md (incl. how each feature is reached by deep link/REST/MCP/CLI/voice and the archived build it replaces); THREADS row; push branch and open PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link

- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.

Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).

Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.

- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.

I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. Approvals and veto notices are guarded: only Brett's own click turns them down, never a session or agent. `python apps/console-web/plugins/notify-control/test.py` fails on an alert source no registry names.

CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).

- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.

The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.

Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).

- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Then show Brett the differences and improvements in chat (phone-readable summary, link to the report).
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. - One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.

- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).

Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.

"If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded).

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator). Build orchestrator owns only Queued and Active (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending); finished builds go back to Build Manager Complete. Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: polished, professional, like a modern SaaS dashboard. One shared visual language across all four tabs (same spacing, type, badges, row style), but each tab shows what fits it; rows may be two lines tall, info doesn't have to be identical or in the same place. Rows expand to collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps, runs, cost, PR, Brett's words, log tail).
- Every row: dates (created, started, finished as relevant), steps total and steps completed.
- Pending: no timer; created date, steps, priority, Send to orchestrator.
- Queued: queue position, why it's waiting, account/model planned.
- Active: animated activity indicator in the row, live elapsed timer, steps complete with progress bar, current step, account actually running it.
- Complete: started/finished dates, duration, cost, account that actually built it, PR/land status.
Theme tokens only, phone + desktop, screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

before.title: File watchdog plugin: watch files, run scripts or console commands, optional AI prompt (off by default)
before.detail: New console plugin. Core runs with zero AI: watch files or folders (paths, globs) on the VPS/repo for changes (created, modified, deleted) using inotify/fs.watch. Add/remove watches by voice, API (control@1) and UI. Each watch has one or more actions when it fires: notify AmberX/console, run a script, run a shell command (VPS, same approval/policy as other VPS writes), run console commands (control@1 / plugin-commands, e.g. open a screen, queue a build). Optional AI action, OFF by default with a per-watch 'Enable AI' switch: Brett gives it a prompt; when it fires, it sends the prompt plus the changed path, event and diff to Claude (account/model picked through the orchestrator's routing and caps, cost logged). Pass changed path and event type to every action. Log every event and action result. Settings per watch: debounce, recursive, ignore patterns, enabled. List of active watches and recent events. Skip non-essential steps like screenshots (mark them skipped, keep the step).

before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

addenda.said: It doesn't have to be a different job for every single action. I can set rules and permissions for each one, like this one's restricted to that, this one's allowed to do this. Every employee has rules. The orchestrator, every headless session, has to be assigned to an employee. Everything has to be assigned to somebody so I can easily track things. ... Give each employee a unique voice accent that can be tweaked. And if you click a button, you can hear the output pane in words and audio, Jim talking to Joe and all that.

And I can say, Jim, read this page, or read that window, or that tab, or container, or whatever. He'll use his own voice and he'll read it out loud. It can be any app on the screen, it doesn't have to be the console. You can say, Joey, read this tab, this Chrome tab.
So we need writers and readers too.
All the employees' information is gonna be tapped into the old one, right? So everything only exists in one true source, one true place.
We're just gonna upgrade and soup up the old stuff.

Actually, no, it's not separate. It is the group chat. This is where the orchestrator will always hand out jobs. This is where they reach out to the employee. This is the group chat. So there has to be a back and forth when somebody replies to somebody else. Only if it's a reply, though. If not, it [stays in the same feed].

Open the group chat in a multi-tab group where you can open a new tab with Jim and John's conversation. You can drag an employee from one tab to another to put him in a separate conversation. You can click multiple people and drag them into their own tab. Filter, sort, all that. The employee list needs to show the right thing: ID, their picture, a link to their profile, when they were hired, how much work they've done, etc. And their skills and tools: we have to be able to assign them skills, tools and personas. That's where their personas will be managed. If that stuff is anywhere else, put it all in one place.

You can also assign them jobs or move their job or fire them, and you select from a dialog of jobs and you can add everything you want. It's a sortable, filterable, multi-column, collapsible and expandable rows. Make it sick, dude. Make an HR department that's off the meat rack.

Then give me a meticulous walkthrough that describes everything they can do, everything going on, all the information about them, where it's stored, how it works, and how everything's linked together to the employees. A powerful, extensive walkthrough that even includes every individual setting. Make it 30 minutes. Make it sick.

In the walkthrough, keep the group chat open as picture-in-picture, with the group chat going on while you watch the demo go around the screen clicking stuff. before.title: One VPS plugin: everything VPS in one place (gauges, banner widget with heat-colour icons and dropdown, cleanup, settings, status)
before.detail: ONE VPS plugin (e.g. 'VPS'), reachable from Maintenance and its own nav entry. 1) CONSOLIDATE: find every VPS-related feature across the console and move it into this plugin as tabs or sections, leaving no duplicates behind. That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. It has its own settings (metrics, mode, thresholds, refresh). 4) ICON-ONLY HEAT COLOUR: each icon's colour follows its level on a smooth scale, white (low) to gray to black to red (high). The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

Uninstalling the plugin removes the column. 5) BANNER WIDGET: drop-down to pick an account; settings choose what it shows (name, number, usage left, API/subscription, email, any combination). 6) FLOATING OVERLAY WINDOW (not a toolbar): small narrow professional window with customizable buttons; editable behavior and sub-menus in plugin settings; resizable, size lock, dockable where the console allows, minimize to main screen, overlay scope (whole OS vs just the console/browser), styleable like any asset. 7) Full API control for everything.

A master switch in the main application settings to enable inline edit mode. Same with navigation menus, toolbars, banners, widgets, every single thing. Part of the plugin gives a monster list of everything changed from axHub's inheritance, reset them individually to axHub's. A master switch in the main application settings to enable inline edit mode. Same with navigation menus, toolbars, banners, widgets, every single thing. Part of the plugin gives a monster list of everything changed from axHub's inheritance, reset them individually to axHub's. Write the contract doc.

Each override record holds the token path, the scope (single item or parent), the token, the value, the axHub value it replaced, who changed it and when. ## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T23:46:07.460Z
> Give Molly and the AI assistant access to the API so she can drive the console, open screens and configure settings. Easy to reach, hands free. A setting in AI assistant.

## What to build
Continue build "AI assistant in Molly + console drives by API (open screens, change settings) + hands-free voice setting" (ai-assistant-in-molly-console-drives-by-api-open) — Phase 2, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 23:46):
"Give Molly and the AI assistant access to the API so she can drive the console, open screens and configure settings. Easy to reach, hands free. A setting in AI assistant."
This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

before.title: Per-agent API control: switch in each employee's control panel; Amber and Molly on by default
before.detail: Amends 3f5775eb. Console API/control access is a per-agent permission, off by default. In each employee's control panel (Agent Manager / Crew profile) add an 'API control' switch (with scope: open screens, change settings, run commands, file/queue builds). # Build: vps-server-gate-no-build-starts-without-an-orchestrator-issued-id

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "VPS server gate: no build starts without an orchestrator-issued ID" (vps-server-gate-no-build-starts-without-an-orchestrator-issued-id) [orchestrator] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.2 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Server gate: every VPS build launch path checks the orchestrator ID registry and refuses any build with no ID, an unknown ID, or not in Queued. Log refusals, AmberX FYI.
[ ] s2 (~20 min) Owner-only override (off by default) via REST/MCP/CLI/voice; show gate status in the console.

Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link vps-server-gate-no-build-starts-without-an-orchestrator-issued-id --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account account-5 (an API key: billed per token, keep it lean) for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step vps-server-gate-no-build-starts-without-an-orchestrator-issued-id <stepId> done). notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.
