The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

split.note: Split by Claude into 10 steps (0 Fable).

steps.text: Find every Molly reference and write the removal list. Grep the repo for molly, Molly, molly-guide and _offer_molly in apps/console-web (src, server, plugins), framework/, deploy/, _claude/ and .github/. Write the list of what goes, kept by name, to _claude/builds/reports/remove-molly-completely-delete-the-molly-add-on-bundle-from-agent-manager-the.md as a draft. Mark which hits belong to the separate apps/molly project, which stays.

Remove the _offer_molly auto-install that runs at start, together with its call site and any startup hook or setting that triggers it. Drop the setting keys that only existed for it, with a one-time cleanup of saved values if settings persist them.

Delete the molly add-on bundle from agent-manager: the bundle folder, its manifest entry in the add-on/bundle registry, its assets and its install and uninstall paths. Fix any import or index that listed it.

Remove the agent-manager UI pieces that offered or showed Molly (cards, buttons, install prompts, help text), plus their REST routes, MCP plugin commands, CLI verbs and voice actions, so nothing keeps a dead API. Update agent-manager's README and help.

Run the molly-guide plugin's own uninstall.mjs --all against a scratch data dir to see what data it leaves. Delete apps/console-web/plugins/molly-guide completely, then confirm node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check molly-guide --after-uninstall passes.

Remove every leftover molly-guide mention outside its folder: doc lines tagged <!-- axf-plugin:molly-guide -->, notify.json and alert registry entries, help/glossary coverage, plugin catalog and instance lists, control@1 targets (if one exists, retire it the way the append-only rules allow), and console tool pins in CI.

Remove anything that pops Molly up on load: console boot code, the on-start launcher, the welcome or onboarding dialog and popup assets, the banner chip or widget, and the console_show/console_open deep-link targets that pointed at Molly. Keep the generic popup/onboarding hosts working without her.

Clean the console's baked copies and generated files. Re-bake src/axf if framework assets changed, then regenerate tracker.json, the glossary catalog, help, and the chrome/help ratchet baselines (counts only go down).

Add a guard test that fails if molly-guide, the Molly bundle or _offer_molly comes back in the console. Then run the CI sweep: plugin-lifecycle check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, glossary catalog --check, notify-control test.py, tracker --check, console typecheck and build, server tests.

Finish the report: what was removed, what was kept (the apps/molly project) and why, the API surfaces removed, and before/after test results. Add the THREADS.md row and a STATUS.md line. Push the branch, open the PR and say in it that no UI was added (only removed) and which deep links and commands went away, then link the build with builds-live.mjs link.

before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

Add an end-to-end test with a fake claude in HOME/.local/bin: launch it through claude-headless.sh, kill it (SIGTERM, 143), run watchdog run, then assert the build was requeued, the slot freed and refilled, the recovery recorded and the notify sent. Run the notify-control registry test.

Write docs and the catalog: a Watchdog section in the plugin README, help entries, plugin.json/command/CLI-header descriptions for the glossary, and the _claude/builds/README.md recovery flow. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Watchdog panel to UI Review with 3 options (layout variants as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), each with desktop and phone shots, in group 'server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck - <date>'.

Finish: run all the checks (check-build-watchdog, builds-store verify, check-builds-store, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check, the unit and e2e tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck.md with before/after and how each feature is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link). Add a THREADS.md row, open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add it to the merge queue.

# Build: banner-widget-shapes-plus-change-icon

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-16T22:59:51.546Z
> Rebuild.

## What to build
Continue build "Banner widget shapes plus change icon" (banner-widget-shapes-plus-change-icon) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-16 22:59):
"Rebuild."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Steps ≤ 10 min.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next (orchestrator.mjs act step <build> <stepId> done; the VPS opens and links the PR). Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~40 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Design the widget shape contract: add a widget-shape@1 field set (shape: circle|square|rounded|pill|hexagon|custom, customPath for custom, iconOverride {pack,id}) to the banner widget entry in framework/schemas/asset-types.json and schemas/customize.json style target, with defaults that keep today's circle; regenerate JSON Schemas (axf.mjs schemas)
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Migration: per-widget settings migrate from the old implicit circle to shape:'circle' (no visual change); write the migration in the banner widget host engine and record the Android twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Widget host engine: resolve a widget's shape + icon override into compiled tokens (--fx-widget-shape-radius, clip-path for hexagon/custom from a token, icon ref), validating custom paths and falling back to circle on bad input
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Fixtures: add golden outputs for each shape, custom path, invalid input and icon override; regenerate with gen-fixtures.mts and extend check-widgets.mts to assert them
Read first: framework/schemas/asset-types.json, framework/schemas/customize.json, framework/schemas/json/, framework/core/engines/, framework/spec/PORTING.md, framework/core/, framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts, framework/spec/fixtures/, framework/spec/check-widgets.mts
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step banner-widget-shapes-plus-change-icon <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). The VPS opens the PR and links it (Build rules → builds-live).
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step banner-widget-shapes-plus-change-icon <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note banner-widget-shapes-plus-change-icon "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.

steps.text: Define the open-url route@1 contract that axHub, the console and AmberX share: try routes in order (connected console tab → full-screen intent or overlay exemption → notification), with inputs (url, host allowlist amberxai.com, foreground hint), the result shape {route, opened, reason}, and fixtures. steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Define the open-url route@1 contract that axHub, the console and AmberX share: try routes in order (connected console tab → full-screen intent or overlay exemption → notification), with inputs (url, host allowlist amberxai.com, foreground hint), the result shape {route, opened, reason}, and fixtures. Pure engine with no I/O.
steps.why: New cross-app protocol used by axHub, the console and the AmberX app

steps.text: Record the Android twin of open-url route@1 as a deferred gap in PORTING.md, and add the contract to the spec index.
steps.why: Cross-port contract bookkeeping for the new protocol

steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

AmberX settings: an 'Open pages' section showing permission status (overlay, full-screen intent) with grant buttons that deep-link to the Android settings screens, plus a test-open button. Built from framework controls and theme tokens only.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

Build the new AmberX APK in CI. On the S26 Ultra (through axHub), run amberx.open_url three times: Chrome in front with the console tab open, Chrome in front with no console tab, and the phone idle. Record the route and result of each run; screenshots go to UI Review → Screenshots under the build's group, and settings UI options are submitted for review.

Run all checks (route@1, console-control, check-theme, check-controls, toolbars, tracker), write the report _claude/builds/reports/amberx-open-url-must-open-page-even-when.md (before/after per route, device results, API reach per feature), add the THREADS row, open the PR into the merge queue, and send the AmberX FYI about the new APK.

Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. API part 3: CLI `node framework/cli/instance-look.mjs get|set|reset|list <kind> <id> [key=value…]` writing the same settings keys through the console API or the hub look document. Wire `axf look …` into axf.mjs and add help text.

Rebake the shared assets and framework into the listed apps (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake`, `rebake.mjs apply` for console-web and the others). Run check-theme, check-controls, check-chrome-assets, chrome-settings check and check-console-control, and fix any findings.

Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (5 left, ~41 min):
[ ] s1 (~8 min) Survey current main for intent and seams: read the archived branch diff (git log/diff of toolbar-widgets-attach-any-banner-style) for intent only, plus framework/core/engines (banner widget host, attach/snap rules), framework/react/tapConfirm.ts, framework/ui/axf.css banner section, schemas/customize.json style targets; write the design note _claude/builds/reports/attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner.design.md (contract, settings keys, addresses) and commit
[ ] s2 (~8 min) Schema: extend the toolbar asset type and widget attach model in framework/schemas/asset-types.json so a toolbar declares a widget slot list (widget id, side, order, banner widget style + shape ref); regenerate JSON Schemas (axf.mjs schemas) and commit
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Reference engine: toolbar-widget host engine in framework/core/engines (resolve attached widgets per toolbar id, apply banner widget style/shape tokens, snap-not-overlap sizing order: sides size to content, flexible piece shrinks first, overflow scroll-snap); export from core index; commit
[ ] s4 (~8 min) Settings keys + migration: per-toolbar keys axf.toolbar.<id>.widgets (list) and defaults; migrate any existing banner-only widget placements so nothing moves; validators agree (core validator + project-check); commit
[ ] s5 (~7 min) Fixtures: add framework/spec/fixtures/toolbar-widgets.json golden outputs, regenerate with gen-fixtures.mts, record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md; commit

As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note attach-widgets-to-any-toolbar-banner "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.

steps.text: Define the open-url route@1 contract that axHub, the console and AmberX share: try routes in order (connected console tab → full-screen intent or overlay exemption → notification), with inputs (url, host allowlist amberxai.com, foreground hint), the result shape {route, opened, reason}, and fixtures. steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

AmberX settings: an 'Open pages' section showing permission status (overlay, full-screen intent) with grant buttons that deep-link to the Android settings screens, plus a test-open button. Built from framework controls and theme tokens only.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

Build the new AmberX APK in CI. On the S26 Ultra (through axHub), run amberx.open_url three times: Chrome in front with the console tab open, Chrome in front with no console tab, and the phone idle. steps.text: Define the open-url route@1 contract that axHub, the console and AmberX share: try routes in order (connected console tab → full-screen intent or overlay exemption → notification), with inputs (url, host allowlist amberxai.com, foreground hint), the result shape {route, opened, reason}, and fixtures. steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

AmberX settings: an 'Open pages' section showing permission status (overlay, full-screen intent) with grant buttons that deep-link to the Android settings screens, plus a test-open button. Built from framework controls and theme tokens only.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

after.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins cover every asset type, at any scope (Nov 7 2026, Brett: "Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry … Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance … A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack … no hardcoded list; add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage."; build `skins-asset-types`, Fable): how a skin reaches each asset type is worked out from `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` itself (skin-coverage@1, `framework/core/engines/skin-coverage.mjs`): every type is a slot unless excluded; widgets and attachables are styled through their style target in `schemas/customize.json` (`parts` on the skin: box / text / icon / items); the few types with no look or that are bundles declare `"skin": { "by": slot | parts | reference | bundle | none, via?, why? }` on their registry entry. A new type with none of these fails CI (`node framework/spec/check-skin-coverage.mjs`), so a build that adds an asset type gives it a style target or a declaration. A skin MAY name an icon pack (`iconPack`). Scopes follow the icon-map model: hub-wide (`skin` on the shared appearance document) → app (`skin.use`, `skin.inherit` = follow the hub) → screen (`scopes["ui:<view>"]`) → plugin (`scopes["plugin:<id>"]`), the child overrides the parent (`resolveLookSkin`); apps stay their own by default. Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Report: `_claude/builds/reports/skins-asset-types.md`.

- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.

steps.why: engine internals: token resolution order over skins

API part 1: console-control addresses for every instance look (setting:chrome.<kind>.<id>.look.<key>, an action address for reset) registered through control@1 with append-only targets at the end. Add deep links that open an instance's Settings → Look (console_show target).

API part 2: REST routes in the theme-manager plugin: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/plugins/theme-manager/instance-look/<kind>/<id> plus a list route. Expose them as MCP tools through plugin-commands, and add console actions chrome.look.get|set|reset|list for AmberX voice.

API part 3: CLI `node framework/cli/instance-look.mjs get|set|reset|list <kind> <id> [key=value…]` writing the same settings keys through the console API or the hub look document. Wire `axf look …` into axf.mjs and add help text.

before.title: Split builds pages (Build Manager = Pending + Complete; Orchestrator = Queued + Active) with a professional, consistent table design
before.detail:
Replaces one-builds-page-pending-queued-built-tabs-remove (mark superseded).

Pages: Build Manager owns Pending (create, edit, prioritize, Send to orchestrator) and Complete (finished builds sent back by the orchestrator). Build orchestrator owns only Queued and Active (route, assign account, hold, cancel/return to Pending); finished builds go back to Build Manager Complete. Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Design: polished, professional, like a modern SaaS dashboard. One shared visual language across all four tabs (same spacing, type, badges, row style), but each tab shows what fits it; rows may be two lines tall, info doesn't have to be identical or in the same place. Rows expand to collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps, runs, cost, PR, Brett's words, log tail).
- Every row: dates (created, started, finished as relevant), steps total and steps completed.
- Pending: no timer; created date, steps, priority, Send to orchestrator.
- Queued: queue position, why it's waiting, account/model planned.
- Active: animated activity indicator in the row, live elapsed timer, steps complete with progress bar, current step, account actually running it.
- Complete: started/finished dates, duration, cost, account that actually built it, PR/land status.
Theme tokens only, phone + desktop, screenshots to UI Review. Full API/voice control.

before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

steps.text: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Tests for each path.
Why is it expiring when it gets a new refresh token every time? ... Okay, we need to do something about that so it doesn't happen.

Convert every existing skin into this form, with no monolithic skins left. 2) APPLY WITH PICKS: when you apply, enable or change a skin, a dialog lists its sections with checkboxes and previews. Drag slices into slots, preview the whole console live, see which slots are empty, swap or clear slots, before/after toggle. Save, apply, export or import as a file, duplicate, edit later. 5) Professional polish: snap animations, slot highlights, desktop and phone layouts. 6) Full control via REST, MCP, CLI and voice (list sections, save section, apply with includes/excludes, build skin from sections, export). Screenshots go to UI Review grouped by screen.

before.title: Drag anything by API and voice (follow-up to full API control, start only after PR #556 lands): every draggable thing (banner widgets, toolbar items, tabs, dock panes, grid columns/rows, list items, layout slots) gets a move command with drop zones, incl. add/remove/reorder banner widgets; REST, MCP

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

origin.said: I want to be able to drag anything on any page, anything that's draggable, I want to be able to drag it. The regular API build land first.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the drag-move@1 contract: one shape for every draggable kind (banner-widget, toolbar-item, tab, dock-pane, grid-column, grid-row, list-item, layout-slot), with source id, target container, drop zone (before/after/into/side), index and add/remove. Write the spec in framework/spec/DRAG-MOVE.md and an asset-types/schema entry if one is needed.
steps.why: New cross-app contract for how every GUI's drag targets are addressed

steps.text: Write the reference engine framework/core/engines/drag-move.ts: validate a move, resolve drop zones, compute the new order (pure, no DOM), and add an open registry of draggable kinds that hosts register into.
steps.why: Engine internals that every app's drag hosts share

steps.text: Add golden fixtures framework/spec/fixtures/drag-move.json covering reorder, cross-container move, add, remove, invalid zone and out-of-range index. Generate them with gen-fixtures.mts, record the deferred Kotlin twin in PORTING.md, and add npx tsx framework/spec/check-drag-move.mts.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the cross-port contract

steps.text: Add the runtime seam in framework/react: a useDraggableHost(kind, containerId, {list, apply}) hook that registers a host with the runtime (rt.drag.hosts) so a move can run without a pointer, and give the existing drag code paths a shared apply.
steps.why: Changes how drag works in GUIs across every app

steps.text: Wire banner widgets into the drag host: reorder, move between banner slots, and add/remove a widget through the banner widget host engine, so it is the same code path as a manual drag.
Wire toolbar items (Toolbars plugin toolbars) into the drag host: reorder, move to another toolbar, and add or remove an item or a dropped hook.
Wire TabGroup tabs into the drag host: reorder, plus move to another group where the host allows it. Also cover the hand-drawn strips that carry data-axf-tab-group (Terminal, workspace panes).
Wire dock panes and layout slots into the drag host: move a pane to a side or into a tab stack, and swap or move layout slots, all through the layout engine.
Wire DataGrid columns and rows into the drag host (column reorder, row reorder where the grid allows it) and give generic sortable lists the same hookup.

Sweep the console and apps for other draggable things (Build manager queue rows, Plan Studio, Pipeline, asset library, banner pop-out) and register each one as a host. List anything left over in the report.

Add the console actions drag.list (hosts and items on the current page), drag.zones (drop zones for an item) and drag.move / drag.add / drag.remove, registered with the full-API action registry from PR #556.

Add REST routes: GET /api/drag/hosts, GET /api/drag/zones, and POST /api/drag/move|add|remove, relayed to the open console through the existing remote-command channel. Add a Python validator that matches the engine.

Add MCP tools to mcp_server.py: console_drag_list, console_drag_zones, console_drag_move, console_drag_add and console_drag_remove. Each move is a veto call with a reason, and the read tools are read-only.
Add the CLI command axf drag list|zones|move|add|remove (node framework/cli/drag.mjs) on the same REST routes, with help text in the header comment.
Add voice/AmberX intents ("move the clock widget to the left of the banner", "drag the Logs tab first", "remove the CPU widget"). Each resolves names to ids through drag.list, then calls drag.move.
Add deep links: console_show / console_open targets like drag:<kind>:<host>:<item>, which open the page and highlight the item and its drop zones, plus a state read of the current order per host.
Draw drop zones with tokens only when a move is previewed by API (Follow Amber highlight). Make sure check-theme, check-controls and check-chrome-assets pass.
Add tests: a vitest/tsx test for each host kind that shows an API move gives the same result as a simulated pointer drag, plus server route tests and MCP tool tests.

Add a Playwright smoke test on the built console that runs drag.move on a banner widget, a tab and a grid column through REST, checks the order changed and survives a reload. Wrap it in agent-slots heavy.
Add glossary and help entries for the drag commands and the drag-move contract, update catalog/status.json and tracker.json, and record the API reach for each host in the help docs.

Final step: run the full checks (validate, fixtures, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/drag-anything-by-api-and-voice-follow-up-to-full.md, add the THREADS.md row, and open the PR, listing how each draggable is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.

Add the same API on MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin-commands for the routes (watchdog_status/scan/run/settings), CLI `axf watchdog status|scan|run|set`, the voice/console actions `watchdog.run` and `watchdog.status`, and a console_show / console_open deep link target `build-orchestrator/watchdog` (plus `?build=<id>`).

Write unit tests for watchdog.mjs against a temp store (AXF_DATA_DIR): killed 143 is requeued, exit 1 is retried, a stale heartbeat is reset, a live build is untouched, the cap sends the build to Pending, a usage limit goes to the next account, idle slots trigger a tick, one FYI per fix, and a second pass does nothing.

Add an end-to-end test with a fake claude in HOME/.local/bin: launch it through claude-headless.sh, kill it (SIGTERM, 143), run watchdog run, then assert the build was requeued, the slot freed and refilled, the recovery recorded and the notify sent. Run the notify-control registry test.

Write docs and the catalog: a Watchdog section in the plugin README, help entries, plugin.json/command/CLI-header descriptions for the glossary, and the _claude/builds/README.md recovery flow. Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Watchdog panel to UI Review with 3 options (layout variants as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), each with desktop and phone shots, in group 'server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck - <date>'.

Finish: run all the checks (check-build-watchdog, builds-store verify, check-builds-store, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check, the unit and e2e tests). Write _claude/builds/reports/server-watchdog-orchestrator-auto-recovers-stuck.md with before/after and how each feature is reached (REST, MCP, CLI, voice, deep link). Add a THREADS.md row, open the PR, link it with builds-live.mjs link and add it to the merge queue.

- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.

The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. steps.why: Schema + contract design for a hub-wide policy setting and the call classification every caller relies on

steps.text: Find where axHub holds veto calls and the hard-coded 90 s countdown (decision #104); replace the constant with a read of the new setting (clamped 0-120, default 10). 0 s = run at once but still log the notice. Commit.

Classifier tests: table of read-only commands that pass and lookalikes that must be held (cat x > y, git fetch && git reset, ls; rm, $(…), docker logs | tee f, git log --output=f). Commit.

before.title: Server watchdog: orchestrator auto-recovers stuck or killed builds

notes.text: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

Retry failed sessions. Crashes and kills are retried up to maxRetries (default 3). A usage limit or account error retries on the next worker through deploy/claude-workers.mjs route. When the cap is hit, the build goes to Pending with a note. The retry count lives on the build, not in memory.

Keep every slot filled. After each recovery, and on every watchdog pass, call pipeline.mjs tick while free slots plus Queue work remain. If slots sit idle while the Queue is non-empty, record that as a recovery cause ('idle-slots') and fix it.

Schedule it: add an `axf-watchdog` cron every minute (with flock) to the plugin's install.mjs and remove it in uninstall.mjs. Mount and add the env in the deploy install script. Make the plugin-lifecycle check pass.

Send a phone FYI for every fix. Declare notify type `watchdog.fix` (FYI, low priority) and `watchdog.gave-up` (alert) in notify.json, and send each through axf.notify@1 to the AmberX app with build, cause, action and attempt. Set `notified` on the recovery record and batch several fixes in one pass into one push.

Add the health@1 check 'Build watchdog' in systems-check. It goes red when the last pass is older than 3 minutes or a build gave up. Its auto-fix reinstalls the cron and runs one pass. A gave-up build becomes a banner item with Fix (requeue).

Add Watchdog settings as a section of Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator (level toolbar applies): on/off, interval, stale heartbeat minutes, max retries, retry on another account, FYI per fix or batched. Stored as plugin settings keys that watchdog.mjs reads.

Add a Watchdog panel in Build orchestrator, built from framework controls and tokens only, in a TabGroup tab. It shows last pass, running builds with liveness, recent fixes (cause → action, attempt, notified) and a Run now toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label). Each build view shows its recoveries list.
Add the REST API: GET watchdog/status, GET watchdog/scan, POST watchdog/run, GET/PUT watchdog/settings, GET builds/<id>/recoveries on the build-orchestrator server routes.
