origin.said: Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (e.g. killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, and send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Never wait for Brett to notice.

split.note: Split by Claude into 21 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Design the watchdog@1 contract in framework/core/build-watchdog.mjs. A build counts as stuck when it is marked running or queued-running and has no live session: the pid is gone, the tmux session is missing, the heartbeat (lastSeenAt) is older than staleMin, or an exit code is recorded (143 killed, 137 OOM, 1 failed, usage limit). For each case, define the action: reset the running step, release the slot, requeue, retry on the same or another account, or give up after maxRetries and go back to Pending with a banner item. Also define the recovery record shape { at, buildId, phase, step, cause, exit, action, attempt, account, notified }.
steps.why: New cross-app contract that decides builds@1 status transitions

steps.text: Add the JSON schema framework/schemas/build-watchdog.json and register recovery records on builds@1. This adds an optional `recoveries[]` on a build, which normBuild must keep, plus the journal kind `watchdog-recover`. Old records with no recoveries load unchanged, so no migration is needed. Show this in builds-store verify.
steps.why: Schema + store field design on the one builds store

steps.text: Add golden fixtures for the decision table (killed 143, exit 1, stale heartbeat, live session left alone, retry cap reached, usage limit moves to another account) and a check script. Wire the check into CI.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Have deploy/claude-headless.sh record each run's end: exit code, signal, account and the time it ended. It writes them to the build's run record through builds-live.mjs (and a run-status file under the slot dir), so killed (143) and failed (1) runs leave evidence the watchdog can read.
Add the liveness probe: framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs `alive <build>` checks pid, tmux session and slot heartbeat and returns JSON. Also free slots whose process is gone (orphan slot reaping).

Add watchdog.mjs `scan` (dry run) to the build-orchestrator plugin. It reads the store, finds every running build, probes liveness, applies the build-watchdog.mjs decisions and prints the stuck builds with cause and planned action (--json).

Add watchdog.mjs `run`, which applies the recoveries. It resets the stuck step to pending, releases the slot, sets the build back to queued through pipeline.mjs, appends a recoveries[] entry under the store lock and pushes it live with builds-live.mjs. It does this idempotently, using a per-build lock and a cooldown.

- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). - Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.

Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).

- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. - Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins cover every asset type, at any scope (Nov 7 2026, Brett: "Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry … Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance … A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack … no hardcoded list; add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage."; build `skins-asset-types`, Fable): how a skin reaches each asset type is worked out from `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` itself (skin-coverage@1, `framework/core/engines/skin-coverage.mjs`): every type is a slot unless excluded; widgets and attachables are styled through their style target in `schemas/customize.json` (`parts` on the skin: box / text / icon / items); the few types with no look or that are bundles declare `"skin": { "by": slot | parts | reference | bundle | none, via?, why? }` on their registry entry. A new type with none of these fails CI (`node framework/spec/check-skin-coverage.mjs`), so a build that adds an asset type gives it a style target or a declaration. A skin MAY name an icon pack (`iconPack`). Scopes follow the icon-map model: hub-wide (`skin` on the shared appearance document) → app (`skin.use`, `skin.inherit` = follow the hub) → screen (`scopes["ui:<view>"]`) → plugin (`scopes["plugin:<id>"]`), the child overrides the parent (`resolveLookSkin`); apps stay their own by default. Every view root and every plugin root is a `<SkinScope>` (framework/react). Parity: Settings → Appearance (Where / What a skin covers), `node framework/cli/skins.mjs use|off|inherit|follow|global|at|coverage|covers`, the theme-manager routes (MCP by plugin-commands), actions `skin.inherit`, `skin.scope`. Report: `_claude/builds/reports/skins-asset-types.md`.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

steps.text: Define the open-url route@1 contract that axHub, the console and AmberX share: try routes in order (connected console tab → full-screen intent or overlay exemption → notification), with inputs (url, host allowlist amberxai.com, foreground hint), the result shape {route, opened, reason}, and fixtures. Pure engine with no I/O.
steps.why: New cross-app protocol used by axHub, the console and the AmberX app

steps.text: Record the Android twin of open-url route@1 as a deferred gap in PORTING.md, and add the contract to the spec index.
steps.why: Cross-port contract bookkeeping for the new protocol

steps.text: Console server: add a console-control 'navigate' command (REST POST /api/console-control/navigate {url, newTab?}). It finds connected console tabs through the existing control channel, sends the command to the most recently focused tab, waits for its ack (short timeout) and returns route@1's result. The allowlist rejects any host other than amberxai.com.

Console web: handle the 'navigate' command in the tab. A console route navigates in place, and another amberxai.com page opens with window.open in a new tab, falling back to same-tab when blocked. Focus the tab, then ack {opened, mode} back to the server. Register the target in console-control (data-axf-target).

API parity for navigate: MCP tool console_open_url, CLI `axf console open-url <url> [--new-tab]`, an AmberX voice action, and a state read GET /api/console-control/navigate/last (last routes and results). Update check-console-control pins (append-only).
AmberX: on an open_url command, first call the console navigate route (console token from existing pairing). If a tab opened the page, report route 'console-tab' back to axHub and stop.

AmberX: full-screen-intent path. Add USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT to the manifest, plus a trampoline activity that immediately fires the Chrome/default-browser ACTION_VIEW intent and finishes. Post it through a high-priority channel with setFullScreenIntent, and check canUseFullScreenIntent() at runtime.

AmberX: overlay exemption path. When SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is granted (Settings.canDrawOverlays), start the browser intent directly from the service (allowed background start). Use the order from route@1: overlay first when granted, then full-screen intent.

AmberX: the notification becomes the last resort only, and every attempt reports {route, opened, reason}. Also check that a start actually happened (activity resumed / browser resolved) instead of assuming success, so a silently blocked start falls through to the next route.

AmberX settings: an 'Open pages' section showing permission status (overlay, full-screen intent) with grant buttons that deep-link to the Android settings screens, plus a test-open button. Built from framework controls and theme tokens only.

API parity for the AmberX settings: deep link (amberx://settings/open-pages and console_show target), state read (permissions + last route) through the AmberX bridge REST/MCP, test-open as an action, and a voice phrase. Document how each is reached.

Systems check: a health@1 item 'AmberX can't open pages' (no overlay or full-screen-intent permission, or the last open_url fell back to a notification) with an Auto fix that sends the phone to the grant screen.

Tests: node check for route@1 fixtures, a server test for navigate (tab present → console-tab; none → falls through; non-amberxai host refused), and JS unit tests for the AmberX route order with mocked permissions. Wire them into CI.

Build the new AmberX APK in CI. On the S26 Ultra (through axHub), run amberx.open_url three times: Chrome in front with the console tab open, Chrome in front with no console tab, and the phone idle. Record the route and result of each run; screenshots go to UI Review → Screenshots under the build's group, and settings UI options are submitted for review.

No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.

A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. steps.text: Read the archived branch claude/own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups for intent only (git log/diff, no merge). Write the design notes for the per-instance look record (instance-look@1): keys rowBg, rowAltBg, textSize, spacing, borderW, borderColor, radius, hoverBg, selectedBg, selectedFg; values are token refs or scaled steps, never raw px or colours; scope key is kind + settings id. Commit the notes to _claude/builds/reports/own-look-per-grid-and-tab-group.md (design section).
steps.why: schema design for a new cross-app look contract

steps.text: Add the instance-look@1 shape to framework/schemas (customize.json style target or a new entry in asset-types.json with a skin declaration), run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` to regenerate json/, and add validators that refuse raw px or colour values.
steps.why: schema + asset-type registry change shared by every app

steps.text: Reference engine framework/core/engines/instance-look.ts: resolve(skin tokens, app overrides, instance look) → scoped CSS vars (--fx-inst-*) for one grid or tab group, child over parent, an empty record = skin, and reset() drops the record. Pure TS with no DOM code.
steps.why: engine internals: token resolution order over skins

steps.text: Storage keys and migration: per-instance settings keys axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.look and axf.chrome.grid.<id>.look in the chrome-settings rules. Migrate any legacy per-row overrides into them so nothing is lost. Hook it into skin-coverage so the type counts as covered.
steps.why: settings-key contract + migration across apps

steps.text: Fixtures: add cases to framework/spec/fixtures/instance-look.json (skin only, partial override, full override, reset, skin swap under an override, invalid raw value refused) and generate them with `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts`. Record the Kotlin twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md (Android is on hold).
steps.why: cross-port conformance contract

steps.text: Make framework/react/components/TabGroup.tsx read its instance look through the engine and set the scoped --fx-inst-* vars on its root. Add matching tab-group rules in framework/ui/axf.css that read only those vars and fall back through the skin cascade, with no var() fallbacks.
Same for the framework grid (DataGrid): row bg, alternating rows, text size, cell spacing, borders, radius, and hover and selected colours from --fx-inst-*. Make sure it keeps fixed cell widths.

Add grid to the right-click chrome block (ChromeContext) so every DataGrid gets Settings… / Change… / Move with a stable settings id (data-axf-grid or the grid id prop). Add the default settings/chrome-grid asset and run `node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs backfill` for the per-app copies.

Add a 'Look' section to the chrome-tab-group and chrome-grid settings assets: token pickers for every look key, a live preview on the instance, and a Reset to skin button with confirm and one undo. Use framework controls only and give every control a level-toolbar level.

API part 1: console-control addresses for every instance look (setting:chrome.<kind>.<id>.look.<key>, an action address for reset) registered through control@1 with append-only targets at the end. Add deep links that open an instance's Settings → Look (console_show target).

API part 2: REST routes in the theme-manager plugin: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/plugins/theme-manager/instance-look/<kind>/<id> plus a list route. Expose them as MCP tools through plugin-commands, and add console actions chrome.look.get|set|reset|list for AmberX voice.

API part 3: CLI `node framework/cli/instance-look.mjs get|set|reset|list <kind> <id> [key=value…]` writing the same settings keys through the console API or the hub look document. Wire `axf look …` into axf.mjs and add help text.

Rebake the shared assets and framework into the listed apps (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake`, `rebake.mjs apply` for console-web and the others). Run check-theme, check-controls, check-chrome-assets, chrome-settings check and check-console-control, and fix any findings.
